properties.name: daysAfterInitiation
properties.shortDescription: Clean up incomplete multipart uploads after this many days. Prevents storage waste.

examples.code:
resources:
  myBucket:
    type: bucket
    properties:
      lifecycleRules:
        - type: abort-incomplete-multipart-upload
          properties:
            # [!code focus-start]
            daysAfterInitiation: 7
            # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: prefix
properties.shortDescription: Only apply this rule to objects with this key prefix (e.g., logs/, uploads/).

examples.code:
resources:
  myBucket:
    type: bucket
    properties:
      lifecycleRules:
        - type: expiration
          properties:
            # [!code focus-start]
            prefix: logs/
            # [!code focus-end]
            daysAfterUpload: 30

properties.name: tags
properties.shortDescription: Only apply this rule to objects with these tags.

examples.code:
resources:
  myBucket:
    type: bucket
    properties:
      lifecycleRules:
        - type: class-transition
          properties:
            # [!code focus-start]
            tags:
              - key: tier
                value: archive
            # [!code focus-end]
            daysAfterUpload: 60
            storageClass: GLACIER

properties.name: overrides
properties.shortDescription: Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.
properties.longDescription: Use dot-notation paths to override specific properties on any child resource. Find resource logical IDs with stacktape info:stack.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    # [!code focus-start]
    overrides:
      MainDbDatabaseInstance:
        Properties.StorageEncrypted: true
    # [!code focus-end]

branches.label: prebuilt-image
branches.shortDescription: Uses a pre-built container image.

properties.name: repositoryCredentialsSecretArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of a secret containing credentials for a private container registry.
properties.longDescription: The secret must be a JSON object with username and password keys. You can create secrets using the stacktape secret:create command.

examples.code:
resources:
 privateImageService:
   type: web-service
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: prebuilt-image
       properties:
         image: registry.example.com/my-org/my-app:latest
         # [!code focus-start]
         repositoryCredentialsSecretArn: $Secret('registry-credentials.arn')
         # [!code focus-end]
     resources:
       cpu: 0.5
       memory: 1024

properties.name: entryPoint
properties.shortDescription: A script to be executed when the container starts.
properties.longDescription: This overrides the ENTRYPOINT instruction in the Dockerfile.

examples.code:
resources:

   type: web-service
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: prebuilt-image
       properties:
         image: node:22-alpine
         # [!code focus-start]
         entryPoint:
           - /bin/sh
           - -c
           - node server.js
         # [!code focus-end]
     resources:
       cpu: 0.5
       memory: 1024

properties.name: image
properties.shortDescription: The name or URL of the container image.

examples.code:
resources:
 encoder:
   type: batch-job
   properties:
     container:
       packaging:
         type: prebuilt-image
         properties:
           # [!code focus-start]
           image: jrottenberg/ffmpeg:6.1-ubuntu
           # [!code focus-end]
     resources:
       cpu: 2
       memory: 7680

properties.name: command
properties.shortDescription: A command to be executed when the container starts.
properties.longDescription:
This overrides the CMD instruction in the Dockerfile.

Example: ['/app/start.sh']

examples.code:
resources:
 encoder:
   type: batch-job
   properties:
     container:
       packaging:
         type: prebuilt-image
         properties:

             - -i

             - output.webm

branches.label: stacktape-image-buildpack
branches.shortDescription: A zero-config buildpack that creates a container image from your source code.

properties.name: languageSpecificConfig
properties.shortDescription: Language-specific packaging configuration.

properties.name: tsConfigPath
properties.shortDescription: The path to the tsconfig.json file.
properties.longDescription: This is primarily used to resolve path aliases during the build process.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           tsConfigPath: src/tsconfig.build.json
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: emitTsDecoratorMetadata
properties.shortDescription:
Emit TypeScript decorator metadata. Required by NestJS, TypeORM, and similar frameworks.

Source maps are disabled for this artifact because the decorator transform and bundler cannot yet compose their mappings accurately. Emitting a map would give production stack traces incorrect line numbers.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/main.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           emitTsDecoratorMetadata: true
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 1024

properties.name: dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle
properties.shortDescription: A list of dependencies to exclude from the main bundle.
properties.longDescription: These dependencies will be treated as "external" and will not be bundled directly into your application's code. Instead, they will be installed separately in the deployment package. Use * to exclude all dependencies from the bundle.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle:
             - sharp
             - "@prisma/client"
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 1024

properties.name: outputModuleFormat
properties.shortDescription: Output module format: cjs (CommonJS) or esm (ES Modules, enables top-level await).
properties.longDescription: Note: Some npm packages don't support ESM. ESM may also produce less readable stack traces.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           outputModuleFormat: esm
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: nodeVersion
properties.shortDescription: The major version of Node.js the buildpack uses to create the artifact. For Lambda packaging, keep the function's runtime aligned with this value.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           nodeVersion: 22
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: disableSourceMaps
properties.shortDescription: Skip generating source maps. Reduces package size but makes production errors harder to debug.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           disableSourceMaps: true
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: outputSourceMapsTo
properties.shortDescription: Save source maps to a local directory instead of uploading them to AWS.
properties.longDescription: Useful for uploading to external error tracking (Sentry, Datadog, etc.). CloudWatch stack traces won't be mapped.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           outputSourceMapsTo: ./build/sourcemaps
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage
properties.shortDescription: A list of dependencies to exclude from the deployment package.
properties.longDescription: This only applies to dependencies that are not statically bundled. To exclude a dependency from the static bundle, use dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle. Use * to exclude all non-bundled dependencies.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle:
             - sharp
           # [!code focus-start]
           dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage:
             - "@types/node"
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 1024

properties.name: packageManagerFile
properties.shortDescription: The path to your project's dependency file.
properties.longDescription: This can be a requirements.txt, Pipfile, or pyproject.toml file.

examples.code:
resources:
 pyApi:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: app/main.py
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           packageManagerFile: app/pyproject.toml
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: packageManager
properties.shortDescription: The Python package manager to use.
properties.longDescription: Stacktape uses uv for dependency resolution and installation. This option is kept for compatibility and must be set to uv if provided.

examples.code:
resources:
 pyApi:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: app/main.py
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           packageManager: uv
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: uvOptionalDependencies
properties.shortDescription: Optional dependency extras to include from pyproject.toml.
properties.longDescription: Each value is passed to uv pip compile as --extra <name>.

examples.code:
resources:
 pyApi:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: app/main.py
         languageSpecificConfig:
           packageManagerFile: app/pyproject.toml
           # [!code focus-start]
           uvOptionalDependencies:
             - postgres
             - redis
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: uvWithGroups
properties.shortDescription: Dependency groups to include from pyproject.toml.
properties.longDescription: Each value is passed to uv pip compile as --group <name>.

examples.code:
resources:
 pyApi:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: app/main.py
         languageSpecificConfig:
           packageManagerFile: app/pyproject.toml

             - prod
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: uvWithoutGroups
properties.shortDescription: Dependency groups to exclude from pyproject.toml.
properties.longDescription: Each value is passed to uv pip compile as --no-group <name>.

examples.code:
resources:
 pyApi:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: app/main.py
         languageSpecificConfig:
           packageManagerFile: app/pyproject.toml
           # [!code focus-start]
           uvWithoutGroups:
             - dev
             - test
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: uvOnlyGroups
properties.shortDescription: Only include these dependency groups from pyproject.toml.
properties.longDescription: Each value is passed to uv pip compile as --only-group <name>. This omits the project dependencies and default groups, matching uv behavior.

examples.code:
resources:
 pyApi:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: app/main.py
         languageSpecificConfig:
           packageManagerFile: app/pyproject.toml
           # [!code focus-start]
           uvOnlyGroups:
             - runtime
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: pythonVersion
properties.shortDescription: The Python version the buildpack uses to create the artifact. For Lambda packaging, keep the function's runtime aligned with this value.

examples.code:
resources:

   type: function
   properties:

       properties:

properties.name: runAppAs
properties.shortDescription: Python server type: WSGI (Flask, Django) or ASGI (FastAPI, Starlette).
properties.longDescription: Only for stacktape-image-buildpack. Auto-binds to the PORT env var. Set entryfilePath to module/file.py:app (e.g., app/main.py:app).

           # [!code focus-end]

       cpu: 0.5
       memory: 1024

properties.name: minify

   properties:

properties.name: useMaven

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

properties.shortDescription: A unique name for this alarm (e.g., api-error-rate, db-cpu-high).

properties.longDescription: type selects what to monitor (error rate, CPU, latency, etc.) and properties set the threshold.

properties.name: metric
properties.shortDescription: The metric to monitor on the Load Balancer.
properties.longDescription:
The threshold will be compared against the calculated value of statistic(METRIC), where:

  • statistic is the function applied to the metric values collected during the evaluation period (default: avg).
  • METRIC is the chosen metric.

Available Metrics:

  • ActiveConnectionCount: The total number of concurrent TCP connections active from clients to the load balancer and from the load balancer to targets.
  • AnomalousHostCount: The number of hosts detected with anomalies.
  • ClientTLSNegotiationErrorCount: The number of TLS connections initiated by the client that did not establish a session with the load balancer due to a TLS error.
  • ConsumedLCUs: The number of load balancer capacity units (LCU) used by your load balancer.
  • DesyncMitigationMode_NonCompliant_Request_Count: The number of requests that do not comply with RFC 7230.
  • DroppedInvalidHeaderRequestCount: The number of requests where the load balancer removed HTTP headers with invalid fields before routing the request.
  • MitigatedHostCount: The number of targets under mitigation.
  • ForwardedInvalidHeaderRequestCount: The number of requests routed by the load balancer that had HTTP headers with invalid fields.
  • GrpcRequestCount: The number of gRPC requests processed over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • HTTP_Fixed_Response_Count: The number of successful fixed-response actions.
  • HTTP_Redirect_Count: The number of successful redirect actions.
  • HTTP_Redirect_Url_Limit_Exceeded_Count: The number of redirect actions that failed because the URL in the response location header exceeded 8K.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_3XX_Count: The number of HTTP 3XX redirection codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_4XX_Count: The number of HTTP 4XX client error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count: The number of HTTP 5XX server error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_500_Count: The number of HTTP 500 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_502_Count: The number of HTTP 502 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_503_Count: The number of HTTP 503 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_504_Count: The number of HTTP 504 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • IPv6ProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer over IPv6.
  • IPv6RequestCount: The number of IPv6 requests received by the load balancer.
  • NewConnectionCount: The total number of new TCP connections established from clients to the load balancer and from the load balancer to targets.
  • NonStickyRequestCount: The number of requests where the load balancer chose a new target because it could not use an existing sticky session.
  • ProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • RejectedConnectionCount: The number of connections rejected because the load balancer reached its maximum number of connections.
  • RequestCount: The number of requests processed over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • RuleEvaluations: The number of rules processed by the load balancer, averaged over an hour.
  • HealthyHostCount: The number of targets that are considered healthy.
  • HTTPCode_Target_2XX_Count: The number of HTTP 2XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_3XX_Count: The number of HTTP 3XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_4XX_Count: The number of HTTP 4XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count: The number of HTTP 5XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • RequestCountPerTarget: The average number of requests per target in a target group.
  • TargetConnectionErrorCount: The number of connections that were not successfully established between the load balancer and a target.
  • TargetResponseTime: The time elapsed (in seconds) from when a request leaves the load balancer until the target starts sending response headers.
  • TargetTLSNegotiationErrorCount: The number of TLS connections initiated by the load balancer that did not establish a session with the target.
  • UnHealthyHostCount: The number of targets that are considered unhealthy.
  • HealthyStateDNS: The number of zones that meet the DNS healthy state requirements.
  • HealthyStateRouting: The number of zones that meet the routing healthy state requirements.
  • UnhealthyRoutingRequestCount: The number of requests routed using the routing failover action (fail open).
  • UnhealthyStateDNS: The number of zones that do not meet the DNS healthy state requirements.
  • UnhealthyStateRouting: The number of zones that do not meet the routing healthy state requirements.
  • LambdaInternalError: The number of requests to a Lambda function that failed due to an issue internal to the load balancer or AWS Lambda.
  • LambdaTargetProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer for requests to and responses from a Lambda function.
  • LambdaUserError: The number of requests to a Lambda function that failed due to an issue with the Lambda function itself.
  • ELBAuthError: The number of user authentications that could not be completed due to an internal error.
  • ELBAuthFailure: The number of user authentications that could not be completed because the IdP denied access.
  • ELBAuthLatency: The time elapsed (in milliseconds) to query the IdP for the ID token and user info.
  • ELBAuthRefreshTokenSuccess: The number of times the load balancer successfully refreshed user claims using a refresh token.
  • ELBAuthSuccess: The number of successful authentication actions.
  • ELBAuthUserClaimsSizeExceeded: The number of times a configured IdP returned user claims that exceeded 11K bytes in size.

properties.name: metric
properties.shortDescription: The metric to monitor on the Load Balancer.
properties.longDescription:
The threshold will be compared against the calculated value of statistic(METRIC), where:

  • statistic is the function applied to the metric values collected during the evaluation period (default: avg).
  • METRIC is the chosen metric.

Available Metrics:

  • ActiveConnectionCount: The total number of concurrent TCP connections active from clients to the load balancer and from the load balancer to targets.
  • AnomalousHostCount: The number of hosts detected with anomalies.
  • ClientTLSNegotiationErrorCount: The number of TLS connections initiated by the client that did not establish a session with the load balancer due to a TLS error.
  • ConsumedLCUs: The number of load balancer capacity units (LCU) used by your load balancer.
  • DesyncMitigationMode_NonCompliant_Request_Count: The number of requests that do not comply with RFC 7230.
  • DroppedInvalidHeaderRequestCount: The number of requests where the load balancer removed HTTP headers with invalid fields before routing the request.
  • MitigatedHostCount: The number of targets under mitigation.
  • ForwardedInvalidHeaderRequestCount: The number of requests routed by the load balancer that had HTTP headers with invalid fields.
  • GrpcRequestCount: The number of gRPC requests processed over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • HTTP_Fixed_Response_Count: The number of successful fixed-response actions.
  • HTTP_Redirect_Count: The number of successful redirect actions.
  • HTTP_Redirect_Url_Limit_Exceeded_Count: The number of redirect actions that failed because the URL in the response location header exceeded 8K.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_3XX_Count: The number of HTTP 3XX redirection codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_4XX_Count: The number of HTTP 4XX client error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count: The number of HTTP 5XX server error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_500_Count: The number of HTTP 500 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_502_Count: The number of HTTP 502 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_503_Count: The number of HTTP 503 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_504_Count: The number of HTTP 504 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • IPv6ProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer over IPv6.
  • IPv6RequestCount: The number of IPv6 requests received by the load balancer.
  • NewConnectionCount: The total number of new TCP connections established from clients to the load balancer and from the load balancer to targets.
  • NonStickyRequestCount: The number of requests where the load balancer chose a new target because it could not use an existing sticky session.
  • ProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • RejectedConnectionCount: The number of connections rejected because the load balancer reached its maximum number of connections.
  • RequestCount: The number of requests processed over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • RuleEvaluations: The number of rules processed by the load balancer, averaged over an hour.
  • HealthyHostCount: The number of targets that are considered healthy.
  • HTTPCode_Target_2XX_Count: The number of HTTP 2XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_3XX_Count: The number of HTTP 3XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_4XX_Count: The number of HTTP 4XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count: The number of HTTP 5XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • RequestCountPerTarget: The average number of requests per target in a target group.
  • TargetConnectionErrorCount: The number of connections that were not successfully established between the load balancer and a target.
  • TargetResponseTime: The time elapsed (in seconds) from when a request leaves the load balancer until the target starts sending response headers.
  • TargetTLSNegotiationErrorCount: The number of TLS connections initiated by the load balancer that did not establish a session with the target.
  • UnHealthyHostCount: The number of targets that are considered unhealthy.
  • HealthyStateDNS: The number of zones that meet the DNS healthy state requirements.
  • HealthyStateRouting: The number of zones that meet the routing healthy state requirements.
  • UnhealthyRoutingRequestCount: The number of requests routed using the routing failover action (fail open).
  • UnhealthyStateDNS: The number of zones that do not meet the DNS healthy state requirements.
  • UnhealthyStateRouting: The number of zones that do not meet the routing healthy state requirements.
  • LambdaInternalError: The number of requests to a Lambda function that failed due to an issue internal to the load balancer or AWS Lambda.
  • LambdaTargetProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer for requests to and responses from a Lambda function.
  • LambdaUserError: The number of requests to a Lambda function that failed due to an issue with the Lambda function itself.
  • ELBAuthError: The number of user authentications that could not be completed due to an internal error.
  • ELBAuthFailure: The number of user authentications that could not be completed because the IdP denied access.
  • ELBAuthLatency: The time elapsed (in milliseconds) to query the IdP for the ID token and user info.
  • ELBAuthRefreshTokenSuccess: The number of times the load balancer successfully refreshed user claims using a refresh token.
  • ELBAuthSuccess: The number of successful authentication actions.
  • ELBAuthUserClaimsSizeExceeded: The number of times a configured IdP returned user claims that exceeded 11K bytes in size.

properties.name: threshold
properties.shortDescription: The threshold that triggers the alarm.
properties.longDescription:
The threshold is compared against the calculated value of statistic(METRIC), where:

  • statistic is the function applied to the metric values collected during the evaluation period (default: avg).
  • METRIC is the chosen metric.

properties.name: enabled
properties.shortDescription: Enable CDN (CloudFront) for faster global delivery and lower bandwidth costs.
properties.longDescription: Caches responses at edge locations worldwide so users get content from the nearest server. The CDN itself has no monthly fee — you pay per request (~$0.01/10k) and per GB transferred.

examples.code:
resources:
assets:
  type: bucket
  properties:
    directoryUpload:
      directoryPath: ./public
    cdn:
      # [!code focus-start]
      enabled: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: cachingOptions
properties.shortDescription: Control how long and what gets cached at the CDN edge.
properties.longDescription:
When the origin response has no Cache-Control header, defaults apply:

  • Bucket origins: cached for 6 months (or until invalidated on deploy).
  • API Gateway / Load Balancer origins: not cached.

examples.code:
resources:
assets:
  type: bucket
  properties:
    directoryUpload:
      directoryPath: ./public
    cdn:
      enabled: true
      # [!code focus-start]
      cachingOptions:
        defaultTTL: 86400
        maxTTL: 31536000
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: cloudfrontPriceClass
properties.shortDescription: Which regions the CDN serves from. Fewer regions = lower cost, but slower for distant users.
properties.longDescription:
• PriceClass_100: North America + Europe. Cheapest option. Good if your users are in the US/EU.
  • PriceClass_200: Adds Asia, Middle East, Africa.
  • PriceClass_All (default): All regions worldwide, including South America and Oceania.

The CDN itself has no monthly base cost - you only pay per request and per GB transferred. The price class controls which edge locations are used, and some regions cost more per request.

examples.code:
resources:
assets:
  type: bucket
  properties:
    directoryUpload:
      directoryPath: ./public
    cdn:
      enabled: true
      # [!code focus-start]
      cloudfrontPriceClass: PriceClass_100
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: customDomains
properties.shortDescription: Custom domains (e.g., cdn.example.com). Stacktape auto-creates DNS records and TLS certificates.
properties.longDescription: Your domain must be added as a Route53 hosted zone in your AWS account first.

examples.code:
resources:

      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: defaultRoutePrefix
properties.shortDescription: Prepend a path prefix to all requests forwarded to the origin.
properties.longDescription: E.g., with prefix /v2, a request for /users is forwarded to the origin as /v2/users.

properties.name: disableInvalidationAfterDeploy
properties.shortDescription: Skip clearing the CDN cache after each deploy.
properties.longDescription: By default, all cached content is flushed on every deploy so users see the latest version. Set to true if you manage cache invalidation yourself or want to keep cached content between deploys.

properties.name: edgeFunctions
properties.shortDescription: Run edge functions on CDN requests/responses (URL rewrites, auth, A/B testing).
properties.longDescription:
• onRequest: Before cache lookup — modify the request, add auth, or return early.
  • onResponse: Before returning to the client — modify headers, add cookies.

properties.name: metric
properties.shortDescription: The metric to monitor on the Load Balancer.
properties.longDescription:
The threshold will be compared against the calculated value of statistic(METRIC), where:

  • statistic is the function applied to the metric values collected during the evaluation period (default: avg).
  • METRIC is the chosen metric.

Available Metrics:

  • ActiveConnectionCount: The total number of concurrent TCP connections active from clients to the load balancer and from the load balancer to targets.
  • AnomalousHostCount: The number of hosts detected with anomalies.
  • ClientTLSNegotiationErrorCount: The number of TLS connections initiated by the client that did not establish a session with the load balancer due to a TLS error.
  • ConsumedLCUs: The number of load balancer capacity units (LCU) used by your load balancer.
  • DesyncMitigationMode_NonCompliant_Request_Count: The number of requests that do not comply with RFC 7230.
  • DroppedInvalidHeaderRequestCount: The number of requests where the load balancer removed HTTP headers with invalid fields before routing the request.
  • MitigatedHostCount: The number of targets under mitigation.
  • ForwardedInvalidHeaderRequestCount: The number of requests routed by the load balancer that had HTTP headers with invalid fields.
  • GrpcRequestCount: The number of gRPC requests processed over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • HTTP_Fixed_Response_Count: The number of successful fixed-response actions.
  • HTTP_Redirect_Count: The number of successful redirect actions.
  • HTTP_Redirect_Url_Limit_Exceeded_Count: The number of redirect actions that failed because the URL in the response location header exceeded 8K.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_3XX_Count: The number of HTTP 3XX redirection codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_4XX_Count: The number of HTTP 4XX client error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count: The number of HTTP 5XX server error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_500_Count: The number of HTTP 500 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_502_Count: The number of HTTP 502 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_503_Count: The number of HTTP 503 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_504_Count: The number of HTTP 504 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • IPv6ProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer over IPv6.
  • IPv6RequestCount: The number of IPv6 requests received by the load balancer.
  • NewConnectionCount: The total number of new TCP connections established from clients to the load balancer and from the load balancer to targets.
  • NonStickyRequestCount: The number of requests where the load balancer chose a new target because it could not use an existing sticky session.
  • ProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • RejectedConnectionCount: The number of connections rejected because the load balancer reached its maximum number of connections.
  • RequestCount: The number of requests processed over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • RuleEvaluations: The number of rules processed by the load balancer, averaged over an hour.
  • HealthyHostCount: The number of targets that are considered healthy.
  • HTTPCode_Target_2XX_Count: The number of HTTP 2XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_3XX_Count: The number of HTTP 3XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_4XX_Count: The number of HTTP 4XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count: The number of HTTP 5XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • RequestCountPerTarget: The average number of requests per target in a target group.
  • TargetConnectionErrorCount: The number of connections that were not successfully established between the load balancer and a target.
  • TargetResponseTime: The time elapsed (in seconds) from when a request leaves the load balancer until the target starts sending response headers.
  • TargetTLSNegotiationErrorCount: The number of TLS connections initiated by the load balancer that did not establish a session with the target.
  • UnHealthyHostCount: The number of targets that are considered unhealthy.
  • HealthyStateDNS: The number of zones that meet the DNS healthy state requirements.
  • HealthyStateRouting: The number of zones that meet the routing healthy state requirements.
  • UnhealthyRoutingRequestCount: The number of requests routed using the routing failover action (fail open).
  • UnhealthyStateDNS: The number of zones that do not meet the DNS healthy state requirements.
  • UnhealthyStateRouting: The number of zones that do not meet the routing healthy state requirements.
  • LambdaInternalError: The number of requests to a Lambda function that failed due to an issue internal to the load balancer or AWS Lambda.
  • LambdaTargetProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer for requests to and responses from a Lambda function.
  • LambdaUserError: The number of requests to a Lambda function that failed due to an issue with the Lambda function itself.
  • ELBAuthError: The number of user authentications that could not be completed due to an internal error.
  • ELBAuthFailure: The number of user authentications that could not be completed because the IdP denied access.
  • ELBAuthLatency: The time elapsed (in milliseconds) to query the IdP for the ID token and user info.
  • ELBAuthRefreshTokenSuccess: The number of times the load balancer successfully refreshed user claims using a refresh token.
  • ELBAuthSuccess: The number of successful authentication actions.
  • ELBAuthUserClaimsSizeExceeded: The number of times a configured IdP returned user claims that exceeded 11K bytes in size.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApi:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/index.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
  publicLb:
    type: application-load-balancer
    properties:
      alarms:
        - description: Too many 5xx errors returned by the load balancer
          trigger:
            type: application-load-balancer-custom
            properties:
              # [!code focus-start]
              metric: HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count
              # [!code focus-end]
              threshold: 50
              statistic: sum
              comparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
          evaluation:
            period: 60
            evaluationPeriods: 5
            breachedPeriods: 3
          notificationTargets:
            - type: slack
              properties:
                conversationId: C0123456789
                accessToken: $Secret('slack-bot-token')

properties.name: threshold
properties.shortDescription: The threshold that triggers the alarm.
properties.longDescription:
The threshold is compared against the calculated value of statistic(METRIC), where:

  • statistic is the function applied to the metric values collected during the evaluation period (default: avg).
  • METRIC is the chosen metric.

ApplicationLoadBalancerIntegration.shortDescription: Triggers a function when an Application Load Balancer receives a matching HTTP request.

properties.name: loadBalancerName
properties.shortDescription: The name of the Application Load Balancer.
properties.longDescription: This must reference a load balancer defined in your Stacktape configuration.

examples.code:
resources:
  publicAlb:
    type: application-load-balancer
    properties: {}
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: application-load-balancer
          properties:
            # [!code focus-start]
            loadBalancerName: publicAlb
            # [!code focus-end]
            listenerPort: 443
            priority: 1
            paths:
              - /api/users
              - '/api/articles/*'
            methods:
              - GET
              - POST
            hosts:
              - api.example.com
              - '*.myapp.com'
            headers:
              - headerName: X-Tenant-Id
                values:
                  - acme-corp
                  - globex
            queryParams:
              - paramName: version
                values:
                  - v2
            sourceIps:
              - 10.0.0.0/16

properties.name: priority
properties.shortDescription: The priority of this integration rule.
properties.longDescription: Load balancer rules are evaluated in order from the lowest priority to the highest. The first rule that matches an incoming request will handle it.

examples.code:

  apiFunction:

          properties:
            loadBalancerName: publicAlb
            # [!code focus-start]
            priority: 1
            # [!code focus-end]
            paths:
              - /api/users

properties.shortDescription: A list of header conditions that the request must match.
properties.longDescription: All header conditions must be met for the request to be routed.

properties.name: hosts
properties.shortDescription: A list of hostnames that will trigger this integration.
properties.longDescription:
The hostname is parsed from the Host header of the request. Wildcards (* and ?) are supported.

Example: api.example.com, *.myapp.com

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: customDomains
properties.shortDescription: Attach custom domains with auto-managed DNS records and TLS certificates.
properties.longDescription: Prerequisite: A Route 53 hosted zone for your domain must exist in your AWS account.

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: astro-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      customDomains:
        - domainName: shop.example.com
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: dev
properties.shortDescription: Dev server config for stacktape dev. Defaults to astro dev.

examples.code:

    type: astro-web
    properties:

      dev:
        command: npm run dev
        workingDirectory: packages/storefront
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: environment
properties.shortDescription: Environment variables for the SSR function. Use $ResourceParam() or $Secret() for dynamic values.

examples.code:
resources:
  marketingDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.6'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db.password')
  web:
    type: astro-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      environment:
        - name: PUBLIC_SITE_NAME
          value: My Store
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          value: $ResourceParam('marketingDb', 'connectionString')
        - name: STRIPE_SECRET
          value: $Secret('stripe.secretKey')
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: fileOptions
properties.shortDescription: Set custom headers (e.g., Cache-Control) for static files matching a pattern.

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: astro-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      fileOptions:
        - includePattern: '_astro/**'
          headers:
            - key: Cache-Control

      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: iamRoleStatements
properties.shortDescription: Raw IAM policy statements for permissions not covered by connectTo.
properties.longDescription: Added as a separate policy alongside auto-generated permissions. Use this for accessing AWS services directly (e.g., Rekognition, Textract, Bedrock).

examples.code:
resources:
  processor:
    type: batch-job
    properties:
      container:
        packaging:
          type: stacktape-image-buildpack
          properties:
            entryfilePath: src/job.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
      # [!code focus-start]
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - textract:AnalyzeDocument
          Resource:
            - '*'
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: serverLambda
properties.shortDescription: Customize the SSR Lambda function (memory, timeout, VPC, logging).

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: astro-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]

        memory: 2048
        timeout: 20
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: useFirewall
properties.shortDescription: Name of a web-app-firewall resource to protect this app. Firewall scope must be cdn.

examples.code:

    properties:

    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      useFirewall: storefrontFirewall
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: joinDefaultVpc
properties.shortDescription: Connect to VPC resources (databases, Redis). Warning: function loses direct internet access.

examples.code:

properties.name: logging
properties.shortDescription: Logging config. Logs are sent to CloudWatch. View with stacktape logs or in the AWS console.

properties.name: memory
properties.shortDescription: Memory in MB (128–10,240). CPU scales proportionally — 1,769 MB = 1 vCPU.

properties.name: assumeRoleOfResource
properties.shortDescription: Assume Role of Resource
properties.longDescription:
The name of a deployed resource whose IAM role the script should assume. This grants the script the same permissions as the specified resource.

The resource must be deployed before the script is executed. Stacktape injects temporary AWS credentials as environment variables, which are automatically used by most AWS SDKs and CLIs.

Supported Resource Types:

  • function
  • batch-job
  • worker-service
  • web-service
  • private-service
  • multi-container-workload
  • nextjs-web
  • astro-web
  • nuxt-web
  • sveltekit-web
  • solidstart-web
  • tanstack-web
  • remix-web

examples.code:
scripts:
  invokeAsApi:
    type: local-script
    properties:
      executeScript: scripts/admin-task.ts
      # [!code focus-start]
      assumeRoleOfResource: api
      # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      connectTo:
        - dataBucket
  dataBucket:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: bastionResource
properties.shortDescription: Bastion Resource Name
properties.longDescription: The name of the bastion resource on which the commands will be executed.

examples.code:
scripts:

    type: bastion-script

          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Connect To
properties.longDescription:
A list of resources the script needs to interact with. Stacktape automatically injects environment variables with connection details for each specified resource.

Environment variable names are in the format STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[VARIABLE_NAME] (e.g., STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING).

Injected Variables by Resource Type:

  • Bucket: NAME, ARN
  • DynamoDbTable: NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN
  • MongoDbAtlasCluster: CONNECTION_STRING
  • RelationalDatabase: CONNECTION_STRING, JDBC_CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. For Aurora clusters, READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_JDBC_CONNECTION_STRING, and READER_HOST are also included.
  • RedisCluster: HOST, READER_HOST, PORT
  • EventBus: ARN
  • Function: ARN
  • BatchJob: JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN
  • UserAuthPool: ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN
  • SnsTopic: ARN, NAME
  • SqsQueue: ARN, NAME, URL
  • UpstashKafkaTopic: TOPIC_NAME, TOPIC_ID, USERNAME, PASSWORD, TCP_ENDPOINT, REST_URL
  • UpstashRedis: HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL
  • PrivateService: ADDRESS
  • WebService: URL

examples.code:
scripts:
  migrate:
    type: local-script
    properties:
      executeCommand: npx prisma migrate deploy
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
      # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro

properties.name: cwd
properties.shortDescription: Working Directory
properties.longDescription: The directory on the bastion host where the command will be executed.

examples.code:
scripts:
  runScript:
    type: bastion-script
    properties:
      bastionResource: jumpBox
      executeCommand: ./maintenance.sh
      # [!code focus-start]
      cwd: /opt/scripts
      # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  jumpBox:
    type: bastion
    properties:
      instanceSize: t3.micro

properties.name: environment
properties.shortDescription: Environment Variables
properties.longDescription:
A list of environment variables to pass to the script or command.

Values can be:

  • A static string, number, or boolean.
  • The result of a custom directive.
  • A reference to another resource's parameter using the $ResourceParam directive.
  • A value from a secret using the $Secret directive.

examples.code:
scripts:
  seed:
    type: local-script
    properties:
      executeScript: scripts/seed.ts
      # [!code focus-start]
      environment:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
        - name: API_KEY
          value: $Secret('seed-api-key')
      # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  table:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:
          name: id
          type: string

properties.name: executeCommand
properties.shortDescription: Execute Command
properties.longDescription:
A single terminal command to execute on the bastion host. Logs from the execution are streamed to your terminal.

You can use either executeCommand or executeCommands, but not both.

examples.code:

  pingDb:
    type: bastion-script
    properties:

      # [!code focus-end]
      connectTo:
        - privateDb
resources:

    type: bastion
    properties:
      instanceSize: t3.micro
  privateDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      accessibility:
        accessibilityMode: scoping-workloads-in-vpc
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro

properties.name: executeCommands
properties.shortDescription: Execute Commands
properties.longDescription:
A list of terminal commands to execute sequentially as a script on the bastion host. Logs from the execution are streamed to your terminal.

You can use either executeCommand or executeCommands, but not both.

examples.code:
scripts:
  dbMaintenance:
    type: bastion-script
    properties:
      bastionResource: jumpBox
      # [!code focus-start]
      executeCommands:
        - psql -h $STP_PRIVATE_DB_HOST -c 'VACUUM ANALYZE;'
        - psql -h $STP_PRIVATE_DB_HOST -c 'REINDEX DATABASE postgres;'
      # [!code focus-end]
      connectTo:
        - privateDb

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions
