properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

properties.name: accessibilityMode
properties.shortDescription: Controls who can connect to your database.
properties.longDescription:
• internet (default): Anyone with the credentials can connect. Simplest setup, great for development. The database is still protected by username/password.
  • vpc: Only your app's resources (and anything in the same VPC) can connect. You can also whitelist specific IPs (e.g., your office) using whitelistedIps.
  • scoping-workloads-in-vpc: Most restrictive. Only resources that explicitly list this database in their connectTo can reach it. Best for production.
  • whitelisted-ips-only: Only the IP addresses you list in whitelistedIps can connect.

Aurora Serverless engines only support vpc or scoping-workloads-in-vpc.

examples.code:
resources:
mainDatabase:
  type: relational-database
  properties:
    credentials:
      masterUserPassword: $Secret('mainDatabase.password')
    accessibility:
      # [!code focus-start]
      accessibilityMode: vpc
      # [!code focus-end]
    engine:
      type: postgres
      properties:
        version: '16.6'
        primaryInstance:
          instanceSize: db.t4g.medium

properties.name: forceDisablePublicIp
properties.shortDescription: Remove the database's public IP entirely (VPC-only access).
properties.longDescription: For Aurora, this can only be set at creation time and cannot be changed later.

examples.code:
resources:
mainDatabase:
  type: relational-database
  properties:
    credentials:
      masterUserPassword: $Secret('mainDatabase.password')
    accessibility:
      accessibilityMode: vpc
      # [!code focus-start]
      forceDisablePublicIp: true
      # [!code focus-end]
    engine:
      type: postgres
      properties:
        version: '16.6'
        primaryInstance:
          instanceSize: db.t4g.medium

properties.name: whitelistedIps
properties.shortDescription: IP addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to connect (e.g., 203.0.113.50/32).
properties.longDescription:
• In vpc/scoping-workloads-in-vpc: adds external IPs on top of VPC access (e.g., your office).
  • In whitelisted-ips-only: only these IPs can connect.
  • No effect in internet mode.

examples.code:
resources:
mainDatabase:
  type: relational-database
  properties:
    credentials:
      masterUserPassword: $Secret('mainDatabase.password')
    accessibility:
      accessibilityMode: whitelisted-ips-only
      # [!code focus-start]
      whitelistedIps:
        - 203.0.113.50/32
        - 198.51.100.0/24
      # [!code focus-end]
    engine:
      type: postgres
      properties:
        version: '16.6'
        primaryInstance:
          instanceSize: db.t4g.medium

properties.name: cloudformationRoleArn
properties.shortDescription: IAM role for CloudFormation to assume during create/update/delete operations.
properties.longDescription: Use this when your deploy user has limited permissions and CloudFormation needs a more privileged role to manage resources. The role is persisted across deployments and reused for delete/rollback even if removed from config later.

examples.code:
deploymentConfig:
  # [!code focus-start]
  cloudformationRoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CloudFormationDeployRole
  # [!code focus-end]

    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512

properties.name: disableAutoRollback
properties.shortDescription: Keep the stack in a failed state instead of rolling back on deployment failure.
properties.longDescription: Useful for debugging: inspect what went wrong, then fix and redeploy (or run stacktape rollback manually). By default, failed deployments auto-rollback to the last working state.

examples.code:
deploymentConfig:
  # [!code focus-start]
  disableAutoRollback: true
  # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512

properties.name: disableS3TransferAcceleration
properties.shortDescription: Disable faster uploads via S3 Transfer Acceleration.
properties.longDescription: Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through the nearest AWS edge location for faster deploys, especially from distant regions. Adds a small cost per GB. Automatically disabled in regions where it's not available.

examples.code:
deploymentConfig:
  # [!code focus-start]
  disableS3TransferAcceleration: true
  # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512

properties.name: monitoringTimeAfterDeploymentInMinutes
properties.shortDescription: How long (in minutes) to monitor rollback alarms after deployment completes.
properties.longDescription: If an alarm fires during this window, the stack rolls back automatically. Only useful when triggerRollbackOnAlarms is configured.

examples.code:
deploymentConfig:
  triggerRollbackOnAlarms:
    - arn:aws:cloudwatch:eu-west-1:123456789012:alarm:high-error-rate
  # [!code focus-start]
  monitoringTimeAfterDeploymentInMinutes: 15
  # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024

properties.name: previousVersionsToKeep
properties.shortDescription: How many old deployment artifacts (Lambda bundles, container images) to keep.
properties.longDescription: Older versions are cleaned up automatically. Lower values save storage costs, higher values make it easier to roll back to previous versions.

examples.code:
deploymentConfig:
  # [!code focus-start]
  previousVersionsToKeep: 3
  # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512

properties.name: publishEventsToArn
properties.shortDescription: SNS topic ARNs to receive CloudFormation stack events during deployment.
properties.longDescription: Useful for monitoring deployments in external systems (Slack, PagerDuty, etc.).

examples.code:

  # [!code focus-start]

        memory: 512

properties.name: terminationProtection
properties.shortDescription: Prevents accidental stack deletion. Must be disabled before you can delete.
properties.longDescription: Recommended for production stacks. To delete a protected stack, first deploy with terminationProtection: false, then run the delete command.

examples.code:

  # [!code focus-start]
  terminationProtection: true

properties.name: triggerRollbackOnAlarms
properties.shortDescription: Alarms that trigger automatic rollback if they fire during deployment.
properties.longDescription:
Specify alarm names (from alarms section) or ARNs. The alarm must already exist - a newly created alarm only takes effect on the next deployment.

Use with monitoringTimeAfterDeploymentInMinutes to keep watching after deploy completes.

    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024

DeploymentScript.shortDescription: Run a script during deploy or delete — database migrations, seed data, cleanup tasks.

properties.name: packaging
properties.shortDescription: How the script code is packaged. Use stacktape-lambda-buildpack for auto-bundling.

branches.label: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
branches.shortDescription: A zero-config buildpack that packages your code for AWS Lambda.

properties.name: handlerFunction
properties.shortDescription: The name of the handler function to be executed when the Lambda is invoked.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts

         handlerFunction: handler
         # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: entryfilePath
properties.shortDescription: Path to your app's entry point, relative to the Stacktape config file.
properties.longDescription: For JS/TS: code is bundled into a single file. Dependencies with native binaries are installed separately. For Python: use module/file.py:app format when using runAppAs (WSGI/ASGI).

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         # [!code focus-start]
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512
     timeout: 15

properties.name: includeFiles
properties.shortDescription: A glob pattern of files to explicitly include in the deployment package.
properties.longDescription: The path is relative to your Stacktape configuration file.

examples.code:

   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts

         includeFiles:
           - templates/**/*.html
           - config/defaults.json
         # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: excludeFiles
properties.shortDescription: A glob pattern of files to explicitly exclude from the deployment package.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         # [!code focus-start]
         excludeFiles:
           - "**/*.test.ts"
           - "**/__mocks__/**"
         # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: excludeDependencies
properties.shortDescription: A list of dependencies to exclude from the deployment package.

examples.code:

   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts

properties.name: languageSpecificConfig
properties.shortDescription: Language-specific packaging configuration.

properties.name: tsConfigPath
properties.shortDescription: The path to the tsconfig.json file.
properties.longDescription: This is primarily used to resolve path aliases during the build process.

properties.name: emitTsDecoratorMetadata
properties.shortDescription:
Emit TypeScript decorator metadata. Required by NestJS, TypeORM, and similar frameworks.

Source maps are disabled for this artifact because the decorator transform and bundler cannot yet compose their mappings accurately. Emitting a map would give production stack traces incorrect line numbers.

examples.code:
resources:

   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/main.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           emitTsDecoratorMetadata: true
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 1024

properties.name: dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle
properties.shortDescription: A list of dependencies to exclude from the main bundle.
properties.longDescription: These dependencies will be treated as "external" and will not be bundled directly into your application's code. Instead, they will be installed separately in the deployment package. Use * to exclude all dependencies from the bundle.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle:
             - sharp
             - "@prisma/client"
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 1024

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: headersPreset
properties.shortDescription: Preset for HTTP caching headers, optimized for your frontend framework.
properties.longDescription:
• single-page-app: HTML never cached, hashed assets cached forever. For React/Vue/Angular SPAs.
  • static-website: CDN-cached, never browser-cached. For generic static sites.
  • astro-static-website / sveltekit-static-website / nuxt-static-website: Framework-specific caching (hashed build assets cached forever, HTML always fresh).

Override individual files with fileOptions.

examples.code:
resources:
  assetsBucket:
    type: bucket
    properties:
      directoryUpload:
        directoryPath: ./dist
        # [!code focus-start]
        headersPreset: single-page-app
        # [!code focus-end]
      cdn:
        enabled: true
        rewriteRoutesForSinglePageApp: true

properties.name: includePattern
properties.shortDescription: Glob pattern for files this rule applies to (e.g., *.html, assets/**).

resources:

    properties:

        directoryPath: ./dist
        fileOptions:
          # [!code focus-start]
          - includePattern: '*.html'
          # [!code focus-end]
            headers:
              - key: Cache-Control

properties.name: excludePattern
properties.shortDescription: Glob pattern for files to exclude even if they match includePattern.

    properties:

        directoryPath: ./dist
        fileOptions:
          - includePattern: 'assets/**'
            # [!code focus-start]

            # [!code focus-end]
            headers:
              - key: Cache-Control
                value: 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'

properties.shortDescription: HTTP headers (e.g., Cache-Control) for matching files. Forwarded through CDN to the browser.

properties.name: domainName
properties.shortDescription: Your domain name (e.g., mydomain.com or api.mydomain.com).
properties.longDescription:
Don't include the protocol (https://). The domain must have a Route53 hosted zone in your AWS account, with your registrar's nameservers pointing to it.

Stacktape automatically creates a DNS record and provisions a free TLS certificate.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApi:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      customDomains:
        # [!code focus-start]
        - domainName: api.example.com
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: customCertificateArn
properties.shortDescription: Use your own TLS certificate instead of the auto-generated one.
properties.longDescription: Provide the ARN of an ACM certificate from your AWS account. Only needed if you have specific certificate requirements (e.g., EV/OV certs). By default, Stacktape provisions and renews free certificates automatically.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApi:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      customDomains:
        - domainName: api.example.com
          # [!code focus-start]
          customCertificateArn: arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:123456789012:certificate/abcd1234-ef56-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
          # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: disableDnsRecordCreation
properties.shortDescription: Skip DNS record creation for this domain.
properties.longDescription: Set to true if you manage DNS records yourself (e.g., through Cloudflare or another DNS provider). Stacktape will still provision the TLS certificate but won't touch your DNS.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApi:
    type: web-service
    properties:

        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      customDomains:
        - domainName: api.example.com
          # [!code focus-start]
          disableDnsRecordCreation: true
          # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: streamArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of the DynamoDB table stream.

properties.name: batchSize
properties.shortDescription: The maximum number of records to process in a single batch.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 1,000.

properties.name: bisectBatchOnFunctionError
properties.shortDescription: Splits a failed batch in two before retrying.
properties.longDescription: This can be useful if a failure is caused by a batch being too large.

properties.name: maxBatchWindowSeconds
properties.shortDescription: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait before invoking the function with a batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 300 seconds.

properties.name: maximumRetryAttempts
properties.shortDescription: The number of times to retry a failed batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Important: If an error occurs, the entire batch is retried, including records that were processed successfully. Your function should be idempotent to handle this.

properties.name: onFailure
properties.shortDescription: A destination (SQS queue or SNS topic) for batches that fail after all retry attempts.

properties.name: parallelizationFactor
properties.shortDescription: The number of batches to process concurrently from the same shard.

properties.name: startingPosition
properties.shortDescription: The position in the stream from which to start reading records.
properties.longDescription:
• LATEST: Read only new records.
  • TRIM_HORIZON: Read all available records from the beginning of the stream.

properties.name: readUnits
properties.shortDescription: Read capacity units per second. 1 unit = one 4 KB strongly consistent read (or two eventually consistent).
properties.longDescription: Requests exceeding this limit get throttled. Use readScaling to auto-adjust.

examples.code:
resources:
  catalogTable:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:

      provisionedThroughput:
        # [!code focus-start]
        readUnits: 50
        # [!code focus-end]
        writeUnits: 5

properties.name: writeUnits
properties.shortDescription: Write capacity units per second. 1 unit = one 1 KB write.
properties.longDescription: Requests exceeding this limit get throttled. Use writeScaling to auto-adjust.

examples.code:
resources:

    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:

        readUnits: 5
        # [!code focus-start]
        writeUnits: 40
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: readScaling

        readUnits: 20

        # [!code focus-start]
        readScaling:
          minUnits: 20
          maxUnits: 200

        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: keepUtilizationUnder

properties.name: overrides
properties.shortDescription: Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.

properties.name: projections
properties.shortDescription: Extra attributes to copy into the index. Only projected attributes are available when querying.
properties.longDescription: The table's primary key is always projected. List additional attributes you need in query results.

examples.code:
resources:

properties.shortDescription: Optional sort key for range queries within a partition.

examples.code:
resources:

    properties:

properties.shortDescription: The main key attribute (e.g., userId, orderId). Must be unique if no sort key is used.

examples.code:

properties.name: sortKey
properties.shortDescription: Optional second key for composite keys. Enables range queries and multiple items per partition key.
properties.longDescription: E.g., partition key userId + sort key createdAt lets you query all items for a user sorted by date.

examples.code:
resources:
  eventsTable:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:

          type: number
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: primaryKey
properties.shortDescription: The primary key that uniquely identifies each item.
properties.longDescription:
• Simple key: Just a partitionKey (e.g., userId).
  • Composite key: partitionKey + sortKey (e.g., userId + createdAt).

Cannot be changed after creation. Every item must include the primary key attribute(s).

examples.code:
resources:
  # [!code focus-start]
  ordersTable:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:
          name: customerId
          type: string

    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/reconcile.ts
      events:
        - type: schedule
          properties:
            scheduleRate: rate(1 hour)

properties.name: dev
properties.shortDescription: Dev mode: runs locally in Docker by default. Set remote: true to use the deployed table.

examples.code:
resources:
  cacheTable:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:
          name: cacheKey
          type: string
      # [!code focus-start]
      dev:
        remote: false
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: enablePointInTimeRecovery
properties.shortDescription: Enable continuous backups with point-in-time recovery (restore to any second in the last 35 days).
properties.longDescription: Restores always create a new table. Adds ~20% to storage cost.

examples.code:
resources:
  paymentsTable:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:
          name: paymentId
          type: string
      # [!code focus-start]
      enablePointInTimeRecovery: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: provisionedThroughput
properties.shortDescription: Fixed-capacity mode with predictable pricing. Omit for on-demand (pay-per-request) mode.
properties.longDescription:
• On-demand (default, no config): Pay per read/write. Best for unpredictable or variable traffic.
  • Provisioned: Set fixed read/write capacity. Cheaper at steady, predictable load. Can auto-scale.

examples.code:
resources:
  sessionsTable:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:
          name: sessionId
          type: string
      # [!code focus-start]
      provisionedThroughput:
        readUnits: 25
        writeUnits: 10
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: secondaryIndexes
properties.shortDescription: Additional indexes for querying by attributes other than the primary key.
properties.longDescription: Without indexes, you can only query by primary key. Add a secondary index to query by any attribute (e.g., query orders by status or users by email).

examples.code:
resources:
  usersTable:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:
          name: userId
          type: string
      # [!code focus-start]
      secondaryIndexes:
        - name: byEmail
          partitionKey:
            name: email
            type: string
        - name: byStatusCreatedAt
          partitionKey:
            name: status
            type: string
          sortKey:
            name: createdAt
            type: number
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: streamType
properties.shortDescription: Stream item changes to trigger functions or batch jobs in real time.
properties.longDescription:
• KEYS_ONLY: Only key attributes of the changed item.
  • NEW_IMAGE: The full item after the change.
  • OLD_IMAGE: The full item before the change.
  • NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES: Both before and after — useful for change tracking and auditing.

examples.code:
resources:
  productsTable:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:
          name: productId
          type: string
      # [!code focus-start]
      streamType: NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES

properties.name: onOriginRequest
properties.shortDescription: Name of an edge-lambda-function to run before forwarding to the origin (after cache miss).
properties.longDescription:
Only runs on cache misses. Use to modify the request before it reaches your origin.

Warning: Stacktape uses this trigger internally for bucket/web-service/API Gateway CDN setups. Overriding it may break default behavior. Only use if you know what you're doing.

  type: http-api-gateway
  properties:
    cdn:
      enabled: true
      edgeFunctions:
        # [!code focus-start]
        onOriginRequest: rewriteOrigin
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: onOriginResponse
properties.shortDescription: Name of an edge-lambda-function to run after the origin responds (before caching).
properties.longDescription: Modify the response before it's cached and returned. Changes are cached as if they came from the origin.

        # [!code focus-start]
        onOriginResponse: cacheTuner
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: onRequest
properties.shortDescription: Name of an edge-lambda-function to run when the CDN receives a request (before cache lookup).

properties.name: onResponse
properties.shortDescription: Name of an edge-lambda-function to run before returning the response to the client.
properties.longDescription: Use to modify response headers, add security headers, or set cookies. Does not run if the origin returned a 400+ error or if onRequest already generated a response.

    cdn:

        # [!code focus-start]
        onResponse: securityHeaders
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.shortDescription: Grant access to other resources in your stack (IAM permissions only — no env vars or VPC access).

      edgeFunctions:

      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      edgeFunctions:

EfsFilesystem.shortDescription: Shared file storage that multiple containers can read/write simultaneously.

properties.name: overrides
properties.shortDescription: Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.
properties.longDescription: Use dot-notation paths to override specific properties on any child resource. Find resource logical IDs with stacktape info:stack.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    # [!code focus-start]
    overrides:
      MainDbDatabaseInstance:
        Properties.StorageEncrypted: true
    # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: backupEnabled
properties.shortDescription: Enable daily automatic backups with 35-day retention. Incremental (only changes are copied).

examples.code:
resources:
  mediaStorage:
    type: efs-filesystem
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      backupEnabled: true
      # [!code focus-end]
      throughputMode: elastic
  cmsWorkload:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: cms
          packaging:
            type: prebuilt-image
            properties:
              image: my-repo/cms
          volumeMounts:
            - type: efs
              properties:
                efsFilesystemName: mediaStorage
                mountPath: /var/www/uploads
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024

properties.name: provisionedThroughputInMibps
properties.shortDescription: Guaranteed throughput in MiB/s. Required when throughputMode is provisioned.
properties.longDescription: E.g., 100 = 100 MiB/s. Additional fees apply based on the provisioned amount. Can be changed anytime.

examples.code:
resources:
  highThroughputStorage:
    type: efs-filesystem
    properties:
      throughputMode: provisioned
      # [!code focus-start]
      provisionedThroughputInMibps: 256
      # [!code focus-end]
  dataWorkload:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: processor
          packaging:
            type: prebuilt-image
            properties:
              image: my-repo/data-processor
          volumeMounts:
            - type: efs
              properties:
                efsFilesystemName: highThroughputStorage
                mountPath: /shared
      resources:
        cpu: 4
        memory: 8192

properties.name: throughputMode
properties.shortDescription: How throughput scales with your workload.
properties.longDescription:
• elastic (recommended): Auto-scales throughput. Best for spiky workloads (web apps, CI/CD).
  • provisioned: Fixed throughput you set via provisionedThroughputInMibps. Best for steady high-throughput workloads.
  • bursting: Throughput scales with storage size (50 KiB/s per GiB). Can run out of burst credits.

examples.code:
resources:
  modelStorage:
    type: efs-filesystem
    properties:
      backupEnabled: false
      # [!code focus-start]
      throughputMode: provisioned
      provisionedThroughputInMibps: 100
      # [!code focus-end]
  inferenceWorkload:

    properties:
      containers:
        - name: inference
          packaging:
            type: prebuilt-image
            properties:
              image: my-repo/ml-inference

            - type: efs
              properties:
                efsFilesystemName: modelStorage
                mountPath: /models
      resources:
        cpu: 2
        memory: 4096

properties.name: value
properties.shortDescription: Environment variable value. Numbers and booleans are converted to strings.

properties.name: dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle
properties.shortDescription: A list of dependencies to exclude from the main bundle.
properties.longDescription: These dependencies will be treated as "external" and will not be bundled directly into your application's code. Instead, they will be installed separately in the deployment package. Use * to exclude all dependencies from the bundle.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle:
             - sharp
             - "@prisma/client"
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 1024

properties.name: dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage
properties.shortDescription: A list of dependencies to exclude from the deployment package.
properties.longDescription: This only applies to dependencies that are not statically bundled. To exclude a dependency from the static bundle, use dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle. Use * to exclude all non-bundled dependencies.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/handlers/api.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle:
             - sharp
           # [!code focus-start]
           dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage:
             - "@types/node"
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 1024

properties.name: disableSourceMaps
properties.shortDescription: Skip generating source maps. Reduces package size but makes production errors harder to debug.

examples.code:
resources:
 apiFunction:
   type: function
   properties:
     packaging:
       type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
       properties:

           # [!code focus-start]
           disableSourceMaps: true
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 512

properties.name: emitTsDecoratorMetadata
properties.shortDescription:
Emit TypeScript decorator metadata. Required by NestJS, TypeORM, and similar frameworks.

Source maps are disabled for this artifact because the decorator transform and bundler cannot yet compose their mappings accurately. Emitting a map would give production stack traces incorrect line numbers.

examples.code:

       properties:
         entryfilePath: src/main.ts
         languageSpecificConfig:
           # [!code focus-start]
           emitTsDecoratorMetadata: true
           # [!code focus-end]
     memory: 1024

EventBus.shortDescription: Central event bus for decoupling services. Publish events and trigger functions, queues, or batch jobs.

properties.name: overrides
properties.shortDescription: Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.
properties.longDescription: Use dot-notation paths to override specific properties on any child resource. Find resource logical IDs with stacktape info:stack.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    # [!code focus-start]
    overrides:
      MainDbDatabaseInstance:
        Properties.StorageEncrypted: true
    # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: enabled
properties.shortDescription: Enable event archiving. Disabling deletes the archive.

examples.code:

EventBusIntegration.shortDescription: Triggers a batch job when an event matching a specified pattern is received by an event bus.

properties.name: account
properties.shortDescription: Filter by AWS account ID.

properties.name: detail
properties.shortDescription: Filter by event payload content. Supports nested matching, prefix/suffix, numeric comparisons.

properties.name: detail-type
properties.shortDescription: Filter by event detail-type (e.g., `["OrderPlaced"]`). This is the primary field for routing custom events.

properties.name: region
properties.shortDescription: Filter by AWS region.

properties.name: replay-name
properties.shortDescription: Filter by replay name (only present on replayed events).

properties.name: resources
properties.shortDescription: Filter by resource ARNs.

properties.name: source
properties.shortDescription: Filter by event source (e.g., `["my-app"]` or `["aws.ec2"]` for AWS service events).

properties.name: version
properties.shortDescription: Filter by event version.

properties.name: eventPattern
properties.shortDescription: A pattern to filter events from the event bus.
properties.longDescription: Only events that match this pattern will trigger the target. For details on the syntax, see the AWS EventBridge documentation on event patterns.

properties.name: eventBusArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of an existing event bus.
properties.longDescription: Use this to subscribe to an event bus that is not managed by your stack. You must specify only one of eventBusArn, eventBusName, or useDefaultBus.

properties.name: eventBusName
properties.shortDescription: The name of an event bus defined in your stack's resources.
properties.longDescription: You must specify only one of eventBusArn, eventBusName, or useDefaultBus.

properties.name: input
properties.shortDescription: A fixed JSON object to be passed as the event payload.

properties.name: inputPath
properties.shortDescription: A JSONPath expression to extract a portion of the event to pass to the target.
properties.longDescription: This is useful for forwarding only a specific part of the event payload. You can only use one of input, inputPath, or inputTransformer.

examples.code:
resources:
  orderEvents:
    type: event-bus
  orderProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-order.ts
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          properties:
            eventBusName: orderEvents
            eventPattern:
              source:
                - my.orders
            # [!code focus-start]
            inputPath: $.detail
            # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: inputTransformer
properties.shortDescription: Customizes the event payload sent to the target.
properties.longDescription: This allows you to extract values from the original event and use them to construct a new payload. You can only use one of input, inputPath, or inputTransformer.

examples.code:
resources:
  orderEvents:
    type: event-bus
  orderProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-order.ts
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          properties:
            eventBusName: orderEvents
            eventPattern:
              source:
                - my.orders
            # [!code focus-start]
            inputTransformer:
              inputPathsMap:
                instanceId: $.detail.instance-id
                instanceState: $.detail.state
              inputTemplate:
                message: Instance <instanceId> is now in state <instanceState>.
            # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: onDeliveryFailure
properties.shortDescription: A destination for events that fail to be delivered to the target.
properties.longDescription: In rare cases, an event might fail to be delivered. This property specifies an SQS queue where failed events will be sent.

properties.name: useDefaultBus
properties.shortDescription: Uses the default AWS event bus.
properties.longDescription: You must specify only one of eventBusArn, eventBusName, or useDefaultBus.

properties.name: sqsQueueArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of the SQS queue for failed events.

properties.name: sqsQueueName
properties.shortDescription: The name of an SQS queue (defined in your Stacktape configuration) for failed events.

properties.name: archivation
properties.shortDescription: Archive events to store and replay them later. Useful for debugging, testing, or error recovery.

examples.code:
resources:
  auditEvents:
    type: event-bus
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      archivation:
        enabled: true
        retentionDays: 90
      # [!code focus-end]
  auditLogger:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/audit-logger.ts
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          properties:
            eventBusName: auditEvents
            eventPattern:
              source:
                - my.audit

properties.name: eventSourceName
properties.shortDescription: Partner event source name. Only needed for receiving events from third-party SaaS integrations.

examples.code:
resources:

    type: event-bus
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]

                - aws.partner/example.com/12345/my-integration

properties.name: inputTemplate
properties.shortDescription: A template for constructing a new event payload.
properties.longDescription: Use placeholders (`<placeholder>`) to insert the values extracted with `inputPathsMap`.

properties.name: inputPathsMap
properties.shortDescription: A map of key-value pairs to extract from the event payload.
properties.longDescription: Each value is a JSONPath expression that extracts data from the event. These extracted values can then be used in the `inputTemplate`.

properties.name: hostingContentType
properties.shortDescription: Optimizes caching and routing for your type of frontend app.
properties.longDescription:
• single-page-app: For React, Vue, Angular, or any SPA built with Vite/Webpack. Enables client-side routing (e.g., /about serves index.html). HTML is never browser-cached; hashed assets (.js, .css) are cached forever.

  • static-website (default): For multi-page static sites. All files are CDN-cached but never browser-cached, so users always see the latest content after a deploy.

  • astro-static-website / sveltekit-static-website / nuxt-static-website: Framework-specific presets that cache hashed build assets (_astro/, _app/, _nuxt/) indefinitely while keeping HTML fresh.

  • gatsby-static-website: Gatsby-specific caching following their recommendations.

You can override any preset's behavior using fileOptions.

examples.code:
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      # [!code focus-start]
      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      # [!code focus-end]
      build:
        command: npm run build

          primaryInstance:

HttpApiIntegration.shortDescription: Triggers a function when an HTTP API Gateway receives a matching request.

properties.name: httpApiGatewayName
properties.shortDescription: The name of the HTTP API Gateway.

properties.name: method
properties.shortDescription: The HTTP method that will trigger this integration.
properties.longDescription: You can specify an exact method (e.g., GET) or use * to match any method.

properties.name: path
properties.shortDescription: The URL path that will trigger this integration.
properties.longDescription:
• Exact path: /users
  • Path with parameter: /users/{id}. The id will be available in event.pathParameters.id.
  • Greedy path: /files/{proxy+}. This will match any path starting with /files/.

properties.name: authorizer
properties.shortDescription: An authorizer to protect this route.
properties.longDescription: Unauthorized requests will be rejected with a 401 Unauthorized response.

properties.name: userPoolName
properties.shortDescription: Name of the user pool to protect the API
properties.longDescription:
The Stacktape name of the user-auth-pool resource whose tokens should be accepted by this HTTP API authorizer. Stacktape uses this to:

  • Set the expected audience to the user pool client ID.
  • Build the expected issuer URL based on the user pool and AWS region.

In practice this means only JWTs issued by this pool (and its client) will be considered valid.

examples.code:
resources:
  authPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /me
            authorizer:
              type: cognito
              properties:
                # [!code focus-start]
                userPoolName: authPool
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: identitySources
properties.shortDescription: Where to read the JWT from in the request
properties.longDescription:
A list of identity sources that tell API Gateway where to look for the bearer token, using the $request.* syntax from API Gateway (for example '$request.header.Authorization').

If you omit this, Stacktape defaults to reading the token from the Authorization HTTP header, using a JWT authorizer as described in the API Gateway v2 authorizer docs (AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Authorizer).

examples.code:
resources:
  authPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /me
            authorizer:
              type: cognito
              properties:
                userPoolName: authPool
                # [!code focus-start]
                identitySources:
                  - $request.header.Authorization
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: functionName
properties.shortDescription: Name of the authorizer function
properties.longDescription: The Stacktape name of a function resource that should run for each authorized request. API Gateway calls this Lambda, passes request details, and uses its response to allow or deny access.

examples.code:
resources:
  authorizerFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/authorizer.ts
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /orders
            authorizer:
              type: lambda
              properties:
                # [!code focus-start]
                functionName: authorizerFunction
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: iamResponse
properties.shortDescription: Use IAM-style (v1) authorizer responses
properties.longDescription:
• If true, your Lambda must return a full IAM policy document (the "v1" format).
  • If false or omitted, Stacktape enables simple responses (the HTTP API v2 payload format) so your Lambda can return a small JSON object with an isAuthorized flag and optional context.

This flag is wired to EnableSimpleResponses on the underlying AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Authorizer.

examples.code:
resources:
  authorizerFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/authorizer.ts
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /orders
            authorizer:
              type: lambda
              properties:
                functionName: authorizerFunction
                # [!code focus-start]
                iamResponse: true
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: identitySources
properties.shortDescription: Where to read identity data from
properties.longDescription:
A list of request fields API Gateway should pass into your Lambda authorizer (for example headers, query parameters, or stage variables) using the $request.* syntax.

When left empty, no specific identity sources are configured and your Lambda must inspect the incoming event directly.

examples.code:
resources:
  authorizerFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/authorizer.ts
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /orders
            authorizer:
              type: lambda
              properties:
                functionName: authorizerFunction
                # [!code focus-start]
                identitySources:
                  - $request.header.Authorization
                  - $request.querystring.apiKey
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: cacheResultSeconds
properties.shortDescription: Cache authorizer results
properties.longDescription:
Number of seconds API Gateway should cache the result of the Lambda authorizer for a given identity. While cached, repeated requests skip calling your authorizer function and reuse the previous result.

This value is applied to AuthorizerResultTtlInSeconds. If omitted, Stacktape sets it to 0 (no caching).

examples.code:
resources:
  authorizerFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/authorizer.ts
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /orders
            authorizer:
              type: lambda
              properties:
                functionName: authorizerFunction
                identitySources:
                  - $request.header.Authorization
                # [!code focus-start]
                cacheResultSeconds: 300
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: payloadFormat
properties.shortDescription: The payload format version for the Lambda integration.

properties.name: clientId
properties.shortDescription: OAuth / OIDC client ID
properties.longDescription: The client ID (sometimes called app ID) that you obtained from the external provider's console. Cognito presents this ID when redirecting users to the provider.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      identityProviders:
        - type: Google
          # [!code focus-start]
          clientId: my-google-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
          # [!code focus-end]
          clientSecret: $Secret('google-oauth.client-secret')

properties.name: clientSecret
properties.shortDescription: OAuth / OIDC client secret
properties.longDescription: The client secret associated with the clientId, used by Cognito when exchanging authorization codes for tokens. This value should be kept confidential and only configured from secure sources.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      identityProviders:
        - type: Google
          clientId: my-google-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
          # [!code focus-start]
          clientSecret: $Secret('google-oauth.client-secret')
          # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: type
properties.shortDescription: Provider type
properties.longDescription:
The kind of external identity provider you want to integrate:

  • Facebook, Google, LoginWithAmazon, SignInWithApple: social identity providers.
  • OIDC: a generic OpenID Connect provider.
  • SAML: a SAML 2.0 identity provider (often used for enterprise SSO).

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      identityProviders:
        # [!code focus-start]
        -
          type: Facebook
        # [!code focus-end]
          clientId: my-facebook-app-id
          clientSecret: $Secret('facebook-oauth.client-secret')

properties.name: attributeMapping
properties.shortDescription: Attribute mapping
properties.longDescription:
Maps attributes from the external provider (for example email, given_name) to Cognito user pool attributes. Keys are Cognito attribute names, values are attribute names from the identity provider.

If not provided, Stacktape defaults to mapping email -> email.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      identityProviders:
        - type: Google
          clientId: my-google-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
          clientSecret: $Secret('google-oauth.client-secret')
          # [!code focus-start]
          attributeMapping:
            email: email
            given_name: given_name
          # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: authorizeScopes
properties.shortDescription: Requested scopes
properties.longDescription:
Additional OAuth scopes to request from the identity provider (for example openid, email, profile). These control which pieces of user information and permissions your app receives in the provider's tokens.

If omitted, Stacktape uses a reasonable default per provider (see AWS::Cognito::UserPoolIdentityProvider).

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      identityProviders:
        - type: Google
          clientId: my-google-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
          clientSecret: $Secret('google-oauth.client-secret')
          # [!code focus-start]
          authorizeScopes:
            - openid
            - email
            - profile
          # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: providerDetails
properties.shortDescription: Advanced provider options
properties.longDescription:
Low‑level configuration passed directly into Cognito's ProviderDetails map. You can use this to override endpoints or supply provider‑specific keys as documented by AWS, for example authorize_url, token_url, attributes_request_method, oidc_issuer, and others.

In most cases you don't need to set this – Stacktape configures sensible defaults for common providers.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      identityProviders:
        - type: OIDC
          clientId: my-oidc-client-id
          clientSecret: $Secret('oidc-provider.client-secret')
          authorizeScopes:
            - openid
            - email
          # [!code focus-start]
          providerDetails:
            oidc_issuer: https://idp.example.com
            attributes_request_method: GET
          # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: emailMessage
properties.shortDescription: Invitation email body
properties.longDescription: The text of the email sent when an administrator creates a new user. You can reference placeholders like {username} and {} (temporary password or code) in the message.

examples.code:
resources:
  adminPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      allowOnlyAdminsToCreateAccount: true
      inviteMessageConfig:
        emailSubject: Welcome to Acme

        emailMessage: 'Hi {username}, your temporary password is {####}.'

resources:

properties.name: properties
properties.shortDescription: Properties of authentication method

properties.name: clientCertificate
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of a secret containing the client certificate.
properties.longDescription: This secret should contain the certificate chain (X.509 PEM), private key (PKCS#8 PEM), and an optional private key password. You can create secrets using the stacktape secret:create command.

properties.name: serverRootCaCertificate
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of a secret containing the server's root CA certificate.
properties.longDescription: You can create secrets using the stacktape secret:create command.

properties.name: properties
properties.shortDescription: Properties of authentication method

properties.name: type
properties.shortDescription: The SASL authentication protocol.
properties.longDescription:
• BASIC_AUTH: SASL/PLAIN
  • SASL_SCRAM_256_AUTH: SASL SCRAM-256
  • SASL_SCRAM_512_AUTH: SASL SCRAM-512

properties.name: authenticationSecretArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of a secret containing the Kafka credentials.
properties.longDescription: The secret must be a JSON object with username and password keys. You can create secrets using the stacktape secret:create command.

KafkaTopicIntegration.shortDescription: Triggers a function when new messages are available in a Kafka topic.

properties.name: customKafkaConfiguration
properties.shortDescription: The details of your Kafka cluster.
properties.longDescription: Specifies the bootstrap servers, topic name, and authentication used by the self-managed Kafka event source. This is required because self-managed Kafka is the only Kafka source currently supported by Stacktape.

properties.name: batchSize
properties.shortDescription: The maximum number of records to process in a single batch.
properties.longDescription: The function will be invoked with up to this many records. Maximum is 10,000.

properties.name: maxBatchWindowSeconds
properties.shortDescription: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait before invoking the function with a batch of records.
properties.longDescription: The function will be triggered when either the batchSize is reached or this time window expires. Maximum is 300 seconds.

properties.name: key
properties.shortDescription: Key

examples.code:
resources:
  assetsBucket:
    type: bucket
    properties:
      directoryUpload:
        directoryPath: ./dist
        fileOptions:
          - includePattern: 'assets/**'
            headers:
              # [!code focus-start]
              - key: Cache-Control
              # [!code focus-end]
                value: 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'

properties.name: value
properties.shortDescription: Value

examples.code:
resources:
  assetsBucket:
    type: bucket
    properties:
      directoryUpload:
        directoryPath: ./dist
        fileOptions:
          - includePattern: 'assets/**'
            headers:
              - key: Cache-Control
                # [!code focus-start]
                value: 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'
                # [!code focus-end]

KinesisIntegration.shortDescription: Triggers a function when new records are available in a Kinesis Data Stream.

properties.name: autoCreateConsumer
properties.shortDescription: Automatically creates a dedicated stream consumer for this integration.
properties.longDescription: This is recommended for minimizing latency and maximizing throughput. For more details, see the AWS documentation on stream consumers. This cannot be used with consumerArn.

properties.name: batchSize
properties.shortDescription: The maximum number of records to process in a single batch.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 10,000.

properties.name: bisectBatchOnFunctionError
properties.shortDescription: Splits a failed batch in two before retrying.
properties.longDescription: This can be useful if a failure is caused by a batch being too large.

properties.name: consumerArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of a specific stream consumer to use.
properties.longDescription: This cannot be used with autoCreateConsumer.

properties.name: kinesisStreamName
properties.shortDescription: The name of a Kinesis stream defined in your stack's resources.
properties.longDescription: You must specify either kinesisStreamName or streamArn.

properties.name: maxBatchWindowSeconds
properties.shortDescription: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait before invoking the function with a batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 300 seconds.

properties.name: maximumRetryAttempts
properties.shortDescription: The number of times to retry a failed batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Important: If an error occurs, the entire batch is retried, including records that were processed successfully. Your function should be idempotent to handle this.

properties.name: onFailure
properties.shortDescription: A destination (SQS queue or SNS topic) for batches that fail after all retry attempts.

properties.name: parallelizationFactor
properties.shortDescription: The number of batches to process concurrently from the same shard.

properties.name: startingPosition
properties.shortDescription: The position in the stream from which to start reading records.
properties.longDescription:
• LATEST: Read only new records.
  • TRIM_HORIZON: Read all available records from the beginning of the stream.

properties.name: streamArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of an existing Kinesis stream to consume records from.
properties.longDescription: Use this to consume from a stream that is not managed by your stack. You must specify either kinesisStreamName or streamArn.

KinesisStream.shortDescription: Real-time data stream for ingesting high-volume events (logs, clickstreams, IoT, analytics).

properties.name: overrides
properties.shortDescription: Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.
properties.longDescription: Use dot-notation paths to override specific properties on any child resource. Find resource logical IDs with stacktape info:stack.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    # [!code focus-start]
    overrides:
      MainDbDatabaseInstance:
        Properties.StorageEncrypted: true
    # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: enabled
properties.shortDescription: Enable server-side encryption.

examples.code:
# encryption.enabled
resources:
  encryptedStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      retentionPeriodHours: 24
      encryption:
        # [!code focus-start]
        enabled: true
        # [!code focus-end]
  encryptedConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/consume.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: encryptedStream

properties.name: kmsKeyArn
properties.shortDescription: ARN of your own KMS key. If omitted, uses the AWS-managed alias/aws/kinesis key (no extra cost).

examples.code:
# encryption.kmsKeyArn
resources:
  cmkStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      encryption:
        enabled: true
        # [!code focus-start]
        kmsKeyArn: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab
        # [!code focus-end]
  cmkConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/consume.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: cmkStream

properties.name: capacityMode
properties.shortDescription: How the stream scales.
properties.longDescription:
• ON_DEMAND: Auto-scales, pay per GB. Recommended for most use cases.
  • PROVISIONED: You choose a fixed number of shards (1 MB/s write, 2 MB/s read each). More predictable costs.

examples.code:
# capacityMode
resources:
  eventStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      # [!code focus-end]
      retentionPeriodHours: 48
  streamProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-records.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: eventStream
            batchSize: 100
            startingPosition: LATEST

properties.name: enableEnhancedFanOut
properties.shortDescription: Give each consumer its own dedicated 2 MB/s read throughput (instead of sharing).
properties.longDescription: Use when you have multiple consumers reading from the same stream and need low latency. Enhanced fan-out consumers are auto-created when a Lambda uses autoCreateConsumer: true.

examples.code:
# enableEnhancedFanOut
resources:
  fanoutStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      # [!code focus-start]
      enableEnhancedFanOut: true
      # [!code focus-end]
  realtimeConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/realtime.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: fanoutStream
            autoCreateConsumer: true
            startingPosition: LATEST

properties.name: encryption
properties.shortDescription: Encrypt data at rest using a KMS key.

examples.code:
# encryption
resources:
  secureStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      # [!code focus-start]
      encryption:
        enabled: true
      # [!code focus-end]
  secureConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/consume.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: secureStream

properties.name: retentionPeriodHours
properties.shortDescription: How long records stay in the stream (hours). Range: 24–8,760 (365 days). Beyond 24h costs extra.

examples.code:
# retentionPeriodHours
resources:
  auditTrail:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      # [!code focus-start]
      retentionPeriodHours: 168
      # [!code focus-end]
  auditConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/audit.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: auditTrail
            startingPosition: TRIM_HORIZON

properties.name: shardCount
properties.shortDescription: Number of shards. Only used when capacityMode is PROVISIONED.
properties.longDescription: Each shard: 1 MB/s write (1,000 records/s), 2 MB/s read (shared across consumers).

examples.code:
# shardCount
resources:
  clickstream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: PROVISIONED
      # [!code focus-start]
      shardCount: 4
      # [!code focus-end]
      retentionPeriodHours: 72
  analyticsConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/analytics.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: clickstream
            batchSize: 500

properties.name: thresholdPercent
properties.shortDescription: Fires when the percentage of failed Lambda invocations exceeds this value.

examples.code:
resources:
  worker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: ./src/worker.ts
      alarms:
        - description: Worker failing too often
          trigger:
            type: lambda-error-rate
            properties:
              # [!code focus-start]
              thresholdPercent: 5
              # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: comparisonOperator
properties.shortDescription: How to compare the metric value against the threshold.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDatabase:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserName: admin
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
      alarms:
        - description: Database free memory dropped below threshold
          trigger:
            type: database-free-memory
            properties:
              thresholdMB: 512
              # [!code focus-start]
              comparisonOperator: LessThanThreshold
              # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: thresholdMilliseconds
properties.shortDescription: Fires when Lambda execution time exceeds this value (ms).
properties.longDescription: Default: fires if average duration > threshold. Customize with statistic and comparisonOperator.

examples.code:
resources:
  imageProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: ./src/process-image.ts
      timeout: 30
      alarms:
        - description: Image processing approaching timeout
          trigger:
            type: lambda-duration
            properties:
              # [!code focus-start]
              thresholdMilliseconds: 25000
              # [!code focus-end]
              statistic: max

properties.name: comparisonOperator
properties.shortDescription: How to compare the metric value against the threshold.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDatabase:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserName: admin
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:

properties.name: cacheResultSeconds
properties.shortDescription: Cache authorizer results
properties.longDescription:
Number of seconds API Gateway should cache the result of the Lambda authorizer for a given identity. While cached, repeated requests skip calling your authorizer function and reuse the previous result.

This value is applied to AuthorizerResultTtlInSeconds. If omitted, Stacktape sets it to 0 (no caching).

This flag is wired to EnableSimpleResponses on the underlying AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Authorizer.

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: deployment

        properties:

  smokeTest:

    properties:

        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/smoke-test.ts

properties.name: destinations
properties.shortDescription: Route async invocation results to another service (SQS, SNS, EventBus, or another function).
properties.longDescription: Useful for building event-driven workflows: send successful results to one destination and failures to another for error handling.

branches.label: application-load-balancer
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function when an Application Load Balancer receives a matching HTTP request.

properties.name: loadBalancerName
properties.shortDescription: The name of the Application Load Balancer.
properties.longDescription: This must reference a load balancer defined in your Stacktape configuration.

examples.code:

            paths:
              - /api/users
              - '/api/articles/*'
            methods:
              - GET
              - POST
            hosts:
              - api.example.com
              - '*.myapp.com'
            headers:
              - headerName: X-Tenant-Id
                values:
                  - acme-corp
                  - globex
            queryParams:
              - paramName: version
                values:
                  - v2
            sourceIps:
              - 10.0.0.0/16

properties.name: listenerPort
properties.shortDescription: The port of the load balancer listener to attach to.
properties.longDescription: You only need to specify this if the load balancer uses custom listeners.

examples.code:

properties.name: priority
properties.shortDescription: The priority of this integration rule.
properties.longDescription: Load balancer rules are evaluated in order from the lowest priority to the highest. The first rule that matches an incoming request will handle it.

examples.code:

properties.longDescription:
The request will be routed if its path matches any of the paths in this list. The comparison is case-sensitive and supports * and ? wildcards.

Example: /users, /articles/*

examples.code:
