branches.label: kafka-topic
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function when new messages are available in a Kafka topic.

properties.name: customKafkaConfiguration
properties.shortDescription: The details of your Kafka cluster.
properties.longDescription: Specifies the bootstrap servers, topic name, and authentication used by the self-managed Kafka event source. This is required because self-managed Kafka is the only Kafka source currently supported by Stacktape.

properties.name: batchSize
properties.shortDescription: The maximum number of records to process in a single batch.
properties.longDescription: The function will be invoked with up to this many records. Maximum is 10,000.

properties.name: maxBatchWindowSeconds
properties.shortDescription: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait before invoking the function with a batch of records.
properties.longDescription: The function will be triggered when either the batchSize is reached or this time window expires. Maximum is 300 seconds.

branches.label: sns
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function when a new message is published to an SNS topic.

properties.name: snsTopicName
properties.shortDescription: The name of an SNS topic defined in your stack's resources.
properties.longDescription: You must specify either snsTopicName or snsTopicArn.

properties.name: snsTopicArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of an existing SNS topic.
properties.longDescription: Use this to subscribe to a topic that is not managed by your stack. You must specify either snsTopicName or snsTopicArn.

properties.name: filterPolicy
properties.shortDescription: Filter messages by attributes so only relevant ones trigger the function.
properties.longDescription: Uses SNS subscription filter policy syntax. For content-based filtering, use EventBridge instead.

properties.name: onDeliveryFailure
properties.shortDescription: A destination for messages that fail to be delivered to the target.
properties.longDescription: In rare cases (e.g., if the target function cannot scale fast enough), a message might fail to be delivered. This property specifies an SQS queue where failed messages will be sent.

branches.label: sqs
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function when new messages are available in an SQS queue.

properties.name: sqsQueueName
properties.shortDescription: The name of an SQS queue defined in your stack's resources.
properties.longDescription: You must specify either sqsQueueName or sqsQueueArn.

properties.name: sqsQueueArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of an existing SQS queue.
properties.longDescription: Use this to consume messages from a queue that is not managed by your stack. You must specify either sqsQueueName or sqsQueueArn.

properties.name: batchSize
properties.shortDescription: The maximum number of records to process in a single batch.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 10,000.

properties.name: maxBatchWindowSeconds
properties.shortDescription: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait before invoking the function with a batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 300 seconds. If not set, the function is invoked as soon as messages are available.

branches.label: kinesis-stream
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function when new records are available in a Kinesis Data Stream.

properties.name: kinesisStreamName
properties.shortDescription: The name of a Kinesis stream defined in your stack's resources.
properties.longDescription: You must specify either kinesisStreamName or streamArn.

properties.name: streamArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of an existing Kinesis stream to consume records from.
properties.longDescription: Use this to consume from a stream that is not managed by your stack. You must specify either kinesisStreamName or streamArn.

properties.name: consumerArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of a specific stream consumer to use.
properties.longDescription: This cannot be used with autoCreateConsumer.

properties.name: autoCreateConsumer
properties.shortDescription: Automatically creates a dedicated stream consumer for this integration.
properties.longDescription: This is recommended for minimizing latency and maximizing throughput. For more details, see the AWS documentation on stream consumers. This cannot be used with consumerArn.

properties.name: maxBatchWindowSeconds
properties.shortDescription: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait before invoking the function with a batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 300 seconds.

properties.name: batchSize
properties.shortDescription: The maximum number of records to process in a single batch.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 10,000.

properties.name: startingPosition
properties.shortDescription: The position in the stream from which to start reading records.
properties.longDescription:
• LATEST: Read only new records.
  • TRIM_HORIZON: Read all available records from the beginning of the stream.

properties.name: maximumRetryAttempts
properties.shortDescription: The number of times to retry a failed batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Important: If an error occurs, the entire batch is retried, including records that were processed successfully. Your function should be idempotent to handle this.

properties.name: onFailure
properties.shortDescription: A destination (SQS queue or SNS topic) for batches that fail after all retry attempts.

properties.name: parallelizationFactor
properties.shortDescription: The number of batches to process concurrently from the same shard.

properties.name: bisectBatchOnFunctionError
properties.shortDescription: Splits a failed batch in two before retrying.
properties.longDescription: This can be useful if a failure is caused by a batch being too large.

branches.label: dynamo-db-stream
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function when items are created, updated, or deleted in a DynamoDB table.

properties.name: streamArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of the DynamoDB table stream.

properties.name: maxBatchWindowSeconds
properties.shortDescription: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait before invoking the function with a batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 300 seconds.

properties.name: batchSize
properties.shortDescription: The maximum number of records to process in a single batch.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 1,000.

properties.name: startingPosition
properties.shortDescription: The position in the stream from which to start reading records.
properties.longDescription:
• LATEST: Read only new records.
  • TRIM_HORIZON: Read all available records from the beginning of the stream.

properties.name: maximumRetryAttempts
properties.shortDescription: The number of times to retry a failed batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Important: If an error occurs, the entire batch is retried, including records that were processed successfully. Your function should be idempotent to handle this.

properties.name: onFailure
properties.shortDescription: A destination (SQS queue or SNS topic) for batches that fail after all retry attempts.

properties.name: parallelizationFactor
properties.shortDescription: The number of batches to process concurrently from the same shard.

properties.name: bisectBatchOnFunctionError
properties.shortDescription: Splits a failed batch in two before retrying.
properties.longDescription: This can be useful if a failure is caused by a batch being too large.

branches.label: s3
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function when files are created, deleted, or restored in an S3 bucket.

properties.name: bucketArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of the S3 bucket to monitor for events.

properties.name: s3EventType
properties.shortDescription: The type of S3 event that will trigger the function.

properties.name: filterRule
properties.shortDescription: A filter to apply to objects, so the function is only triggered for relevant objects.

branches.label: schedule
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function on a recurring schedule (cron jobs, periodic tasks).

properties.name: scheduleRate
properties.shortDescription: The schedule rate or cron expression.
properties.longDescription: Examples: rate(2 hours), cron(0 10 * * ? *)

properties.name: input
properties.shortDescription: A fixed JSON object to be passed as the event payload.

properties.name: inputPath
properties.shortDescription: A JSONPath expression to extract a portion of the event to pass to the target.
properties.longDescription: This is useful for forwarding only a specific part of the event payload. You can only use one of input, inputPath, or inputTransformer.

examples.code:
resources:
  reportFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/report.ts
      events:
        - type: schedule
          properties:
            scheduleRate: rate(1 hour)
            # [!code focus-start]
            inputPath: $.detail
            # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: inputTransformer
properties.shortDescription: Customizes the event payload sent to the target.
properties.longDescription: This allows you to extract values from the original event and use them to construct a new payload. You can only use one of input, inputPath, or inputTransformer.

examples.code:
resources:
  reportFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/report.ts
      events:
        - type: schedule
          properties:
            scheduleRate: rate(1 hour)
            # [!code focus-start]
            inputTransformer:
              inputPathsMap:
                eventTime: $.time
              inputTemplate:
                message: This event occurred at <eventTime>.
            # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: alarmName
properties.shortDescription: The name of the alarm (defined in the alarms section) that will trigger the function.

branches.label: cloudwatch-log
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function when new log records appear in a CloudWatch log group.

properties.name: logGroupArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of the log group to watch for new records.

properties.name: filter
properties.shortDescription: A filter pattern to apply to the log records.
properties.longDescription: Only logs that match this pattern will trigger the function. For details on the syntax, see the AWS documentation on filter and pattern syntax.

branches.label: http-api-gateway
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a function when an HTTP API Gateway receives a matching request.

properties.name: httpApiGatewayName
properties.shortDescription: The name of the HTTP API Gateway.

properties.name: method
properties.shortDescription: The HTTP method that will trigger this integration.
properties.longDescription: You can specify an exact method (e.g., GET) or use * to match any method.

properties.name: path
properties.shortDescription: The URL path that will trigger this integration.
properties.longDescription:
• Exact path: /users
  • Path with parameter: /users/{id}. The id will be available in event.pathParameters.id.
  • Greedy path: /files/{proxy+}. This will match any path starting with /files/.

properties.name: authorizer
properties.shortDescription: An authorizer to protect this route.
properties.longDescription: Unauthorized requests will be rejected with a 401 Unauthorized response.

properties.name: userPoolName
properties.shortDescription: Name of the user pool to protect the API
properties.longDescription:
The Stacktape name of the user-auth-pool resource whose tokens should be accepted by this HTTP API authorizer. Stacktape uses this to:

  • Set the expected audience to the user pool client ID.
  • Build the expected issuer URL based on the user pool and AWS region.

In practice this means only JWTs issued by this pool (and its client) will be considered valid.

examples.code:
resources:
  authPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /me
            authorizer:
              type: cognito
              properties:
                # [!code focus-start]
                userPoolName: authPool
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: identitySources
properties.shortDescription: Where to read the JWT from in the request
properties.longDescription:
A list of identity sources that tell API Gateway where to look for the bearer token, using the $request.* syntax from API Gateway (for example '$request.header.Authorization').

If you omit this, Stacktape defaults to reading the token from the Authorization HTTP header, using a JWT authorizer as described in the API Gateway v2 authorizer docs (AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Authorizer).

examples.code:
resources:
  authPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /me
            authorizer:
              type: cognito
              properties:
                userPoolName: authPool
                # [!code focus-start]
                identitySources:
                  - $request.header.Authorization
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: functionName
properties.shortDescription: Name of the authorizer function
properties.longDescription: The Stacktape name of a function resource that should run for each authorized request. API Gateway calls this Lambda, passes request details, and uses its response to allow or deny access.

examples.code:
resources:
  authorizerFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/authorizer.ts
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /orders
            authorizer:
              type: lambda
              properties:
                # [!code focus-start]
                functionName: authorizerFunction
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: iamResponse
properties.shortDescription: Use IAM-style (v1) authorizer responses
properties.longDescription:
• If true, your Lambda must return a full IAM policy document (the "v1" format).
  • If false or omitted, Stacktape enables simple responses (the HTTP API v2 payload format) so your Lambda can return a small JSON object with an isAuthorized flag and optional context.

This flag is wired to EnableSimpleResponses on the underlying AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Authorizer.

examples.code:
resources:
  authorizerFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/authorizer.ts
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /orders
            authorizer:
              type: lambda
              properties:
                functionName: authorizerFunction
                # [!code focus-start]
                iamResponse: true
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: identitySources
properties.shortDescription: Where to read identity data from
properties.longDescription:
A list of request fields API Gateway should pass into your Lambda authorizer (for example headers, query parameters, or stage variables) using the $request.* syntax.

When left empty, no specific identity sources are configured and your Lambda must inspect the incoming event directly.

examples.code:
resources:
  authorizerFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/authorizer.ts
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /orders
            authorizer:
              type: lambda
              properties:
                functionName: authorizerFunction
                # [!code focus-start]
                identitySources:
                  - $request.header.Authorization
                  - $request.querystring.apiKey
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: cacheResultSeconds
properties.shortDescription: Cache authorizer results
properties.longDescription:
Number of seconds API Gateway should cache the result of the Lambda authorizer for a given identity. While cached, repeated requests skip calling your authorizer function and reuse the previous result.

This value is applied to AuthorizerResultTtlInSeconds. If omitted, Stacktape sets it to 0 (no caching).

examples.code:
resources:
  authorizerFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/authorizer.ts
  httpApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: httpApi
            method: GET
            path: /orders
            authorizer:
              type: lambda
              properties:
                functionName: authorizerFunction
                identitySources:
                  - $request.header.Authorization
                # [!code focus-start]
                cacheResultSeconds: 300
                # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: payloadFormat
properties.shortDescription: The payload format version for the Lambda integration.
properties.longDescription: For details on the differences between formats, see the AWS documentation.

branches.label: event-bus
branches.shortDescription: Triggers a batch job when an event matching a specified pattern is received by an event bus.

properties.name: eventBusArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of an existing event bus.
properties.longDescription: Use this to subscribe to an event bus that is not managed by your stack. You must specify only one of eventBusArn, eventBusName, or useDefaultBus.

properties.name: eventBusName
properties.shortDescription: The name of an event bus defined in your stack's resources.
properties.longDescription: You must specify only one of eventBusArn, eventBusName, or useDefaultBus.

properties.name: useDefaultBus
properties.shortDescription: Uses the default AWS event bus.
properties.longDescription: You must specify only one of eventBusArn, eventBusName, or useDefaultBus.

properties.name: eventPattern
properties.shortDescription: A pattern to filter events from the event bus.
properties.longDescription: Only events that match this pattern will trigger the target. For details on the syntax, see the AWS EventBridge documentation on event patterns.

properties.name: onDeliveryFailure
properties.shortDescription: A destination for events that fail to be delivered to the target.
properties.longDescription: In rare cases, an event might fail to be delivered. This property specifies an SQS queue where failed events will be sent.

properties.name: input
properties.shortDescription: A fixed JSON object to be passed as the event payload.

properties.name: inputPath
properties.shortDescription: A JSONPath expression to extract a portion of the event to pass to the target.
properties.longDescription: This is useful for forwarding only a specific part of the event payload. You can only use one of input, inputPath, or inputTransformer.

examples.code:
resources:
  orderEvents:
    type: event-bus
  orderProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-order.ts
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          properties:
            eventBusName: orderEvents
            eventPattern:
              source:
                - my.orders
            # [!code focus-start]
            inputPath: $.detail
            # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: inputTransformer
properties.shortDescription: Customizes the event payload sent to the target.
properties.longDescription: This allows you to extract values from the original event and use them to construct a new payload. You can only use one of input, inputPath, or inputTransformer.

examples.code:
resources:
  orderEvents:
    type: event-bus
  orderProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-order.ts
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          properties:
            eventBusName: orderEvents
            eventPattern:
              source:
                - my.orders
            # [!code focus-start]
            inputTransformer:
              inputPathsMap:
                instanceId: $.detail.instance-id
                instanceState: $.detail.state
              inputTemplate:
                message: Instance <instanceId> is now in state <instanceState>.
            # [!code focus-end]

resources:
  ordersApi:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/orders.ts
      # [!code focus-start]
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: publicApi
            method: POST
            path: /orders
        - type: schedule
          properties:
            scheduleRate: rate(1 hour)
      # [!code focus-end]
  publicApi:
    type: http-api-gateway

properties.name: iamRoleStatements
properties.shortDescription: Raw IAM policy statements for permissions not covered by connectTo.
properties.longDescription: Added as a separate policy alongside auto-generated permissions. Use this for accessing AWS services directly (e.g., Rekognition, Textract, Bedrock).

examples.code:
resources:
  processor:
    type: batch-job
    properties:
      container:
        packaging:
          type: stacktape-image-buildpack
          properties:
            entryfilePath: src/job.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
      # [!code focus-start]
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - textract:AnalyzeDocument
          Resource:
            - '*'
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: joinDefaultVpc
properties.shortDescription: Connects the function to your VPC so it can reach databases, Redis, and other VPC-only resources.
properties.longDescription:
Set this to true when the function must reach VPC-only resources such as a database with accessibilityMode: 'vpc'/'scoping-workloads-in-vpc', a Redis cluster, or EFS.

Tradeoff: The function loses direct internet access. It can still reach S3 and DynamoDB (Stacktape auto-creates VPC endpoints), but calls to external APIs (Stripe, OpenAI, etc.) will fail. If you need both VPC access and internet, use a web-service or worker-service instead.

Required when using volumeMounts (EFS or S3 Files).

examples.code:
resources:
  dbMigrator:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/migrate.ts
      # [!code focus-start]
      joinDefaultVpc: true
      # [!code focus-end]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro

properties.name: layers
properties.shortDescription: Lambda Layer ARNs to attach (shared libraries, custom runtimes, etc.).
properties.longDescription: Layers are zip archives with additional code/data mounted into the function. Provide the layer ARN (e.g., from AWS console or another stack). Max 5 layers per function.

examples.code:
resources:
  monitoredFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/handler.ts
      # [!code focus-start]
      layers:
        - arn:aws:lambda:eu-west-1:464622532012:layer:Datadog-Extension:62
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: logging
properties.shortDescription: Logging configuration (retention, forwarding).
properties.longDescription: Logs (stdout/stderr) are auto-sent to CloudWatch. View with stacktape logs or in the Stacktape Console.

examples.code:
resources:
  apiHandler:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      # [!code focus-start]
      logging:
        retentionDays: 30
        logForwarding:
          type: datadog
          properties:
            apiKey: $Secret('datadog-api-key')
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: memory
properties.shortDescription: Memory in MB (128 - 10,240). Also determines CPU power.
properties.longDescription: Lambda scales CPU proportionally to memory: 1,769 MB = 1 vCPU, 3,538 MB = 2 vCPUs, etc. If your function is slow, increasing memory gives it more CPU, which often makes it faster and cheaper overall (less execution time).

examples.code:
resources:
  pdfRenderer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/pdf.ts
      # [!code focus-start]
      memory: 3538
      # [!code focus-end]
      timeout: 120

properties.name: provisionedConcurrency
properties.shortDescription: Eliminates cold starts by keeping function instances warm and ready.
properties.longDescription:
When a function hasn't been called recently, the first request can take 1-5+ seconds ("cold start"). This setting pre-warms the specified number of instances so they respond instantly.

When to use: User-facing APIs, web/mobile backends, or any function where response time matters. Skip this for background jobs, cron tasks, or data pipelines.

Cost: You pay for each provisioned instance even when idle. Also increases deploy time by ~2-5 minutes.

examples.code:
resources:
  checkoutApi:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/checkout.ts
      memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      provisionedConcurrency: 5
      # [!code focus-end]
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: storeApi
            method: POST
            path: /checkout
  storeApi:
    type: http-api-gateway

properties.name: reservedConcurrency
properties.shortDescription: Cap the maximum number of concurrent instances for this function.
properties.longDescription:
Reserves this many execution slots exclusively for this function — other functions can't use them, and this function can't scale beyond it. No additional cost.

Common uses:

  • Prevent overwhelming a database with too many connections
  • Guarantee capacity for critical functions
  • Throttle expensive downstream API calls

examples.code:
resources:
  legacyDbWriter:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/write.ts
      # [!code focus-start]
      reservedConcurrency: 10
      # [!code focus-end]
      connectTo:
        - legacyDb
  legacyDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro

properties.name: runtime
properties.shortDescription: The language runtime (e.g., nodejs22.x, python3.13).
properties.longDescription: Auto-detected from your source file extension when using stacktape-lambda-buildpack. Override only if you need a specific version.

properties.shortDescription: Size of the /tmp directory in MB (512 - 10,240). Ephemeral per invocation.
properties.longDescription: Increase if your function downloads/processes large files temporarily.

properties.shortDescription: Max execution time in seconds. Function is killed if it exceeds this.

properties.shortDescription: Give this function its own HTTPS URL (no API Gateway needed).

properties.name: volumeMounts
properties.shortDescription: Persistent file-system mounts shared across invocations and functions.
properties.longDescription: Unlike /tmp, mounted file systems persist independently from the function runtime and can be shared across multiple functions. Requires joinDefaultVpc: true (Stacktape will remind you if you forget).

properties.name: efsFilesystemName

properties.name: properties
properties.shortDescription: Configures where to redirect the request.
properties.longDescription:
A redirect changes the URI, which has the format: protocol://hostname:port/path?query. Unmodified URI components will retain their original values.

To avoid redirect loops, ensure that you sufficiently modify the URI. You can reuse URI components with the following keywords: #{protocol}, #{host}, #{port}, #{path} (the leading / is removed), and #{query}.

For example, you can change the path to /new/#{path}, the hostname to example.#{host}, or the query to #{query}&value=xyz.

examples.code:
resources:
  webLoadBalancer:
    type: application-load-balancer
    properties:
      customDomains:
        - domainName: example.com
        - domainName: www.example.com
      listeners:
        - protocol: HTTPS
          port: 443
          defaultAction:
            type: redirect
            # [!code focus-start]
            properties:
              host: www.example.com
              path: /#{path}
              query: '#{query}'

properties.name: assumeRoleOfResource
properties.shortDescription: Assume Role of Resource
properties.longDescription:
The name of a deployed resource whose IAM role the script should assume. This grants the script the same permissions as the specified resource.

The resource must be deployed before the script is executed. Stacktape injects temporary AWS credentials as environment variables, which are automatically used by most AWS SDKs and CLIs.

Supported Resource Types:

  • function
  • batch-job
  • worker-service
  • web-service
  • private-service
  • multi-container-workload
  • nextjs-web
  • astro-web
  • nuxt-web
  • sveltekit-web
  • solidstart-web
  • tanstack-web
  • remix-web

examples.code:
scripts:
  invokeAsApi:
    type: local-script
    properties:
      executeScript: scripts/admin-task.ts
      # [!code focus-start]
      assumeRoleOfResource: api
      # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      connectTo:
        - dataBucket
  dataBucket:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Connect To
properties.longDescription:
A list of resources the script needs to interact with. Stacktape automatically injects environment variables with connection details for each specified resource.

Environment variable names are in the format STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[VARIABLE_NAME] (e.g., STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING).

Injected Variables by Resource Type:

  • Bucket: NAME, ARN
  • DynamoDbTable: NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN
  • MongoDbAtlasCluster: CONNECTION_STRING
  • RelationalDatabase: CONNECTION_STRING, JDBC_CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. For Aurora clusters, READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_JDBC_CONNECTION_STRING, and READER_HOST are also included.
  • RedisCluster: HOST, READER_HOST, PORT
  • EventBus: ARN
  • Function: ARN
  • BatchJob: JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN
  • UserAuthPool: ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN
  • SnsTopic: ARN, NAME
  • SqsQueue: ARN, NAME, URL
  • UpstashKafkaTopic: TOPIC_NAME, TOPIC_ID, USERNAME, PASSWORD, TCP_ENDPOINT, REST_URL
  • UpstashRedis: HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL
  • PrivateService: ADDRESS
  • WebService: URL

examples.code:
scripts:
  migrate:
    type: local-script
    properties:
      executeCommand: npx prisma migrate deploy
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
      # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro

properties.name: enabledTypes
properties.shortDescription: Enabled MFA factor types
properties.longDescription:
Chooses which MFA methods users can use:

  • SMS: One‑time codes are sent via text message. Requires an SNS role so Cognito can send SMS.
  • SOFTWARE_TOKEN: Time‑based one‑time codes from an authenticator app.
  • EMAIL_OTP: Codes are sent by email. AWS requires that you configure a developer email sending identity (which Stacktape does when you provide emailConfiguration.sesAddressArn).

These values are mapped to Cognito's EnabledMfas setting (SMS_MFA, SOFTWARE_TOKEN_MFA, EMAIL_OTP), whose behavior is described in EnabledMfas in the AWS::Cognito::UserPool docs.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      mfaConfiguration:
        status: OPTIONAL
        # [!code focus-start]
        enabledTypes:
          - SOFTWARE_TOKEN
          - SMS
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: status
properties.shortDescription:
MFA requirement

  • OFF: MFA is completely disabled.
  • ON: All users must complete MFA during sign‑in.
  • OPTIONAL: Users can opt in to MFA; it's recommended but not strictly required.

This value configures the Cognito MfaConfiguration property.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      mfaConfiguration:
        # [!code focus-start]
        status: ON
        # [!code focus-end]
        enabledTypes:
          - SOFTWARE_TOKEN

properties.name: accessibilityMode
properties.shortDescription: Network access mode.
properties.longDescription:
• internet: Accessible from anywhere (credentials still required).
  • vpc: Only from resources in your VPC + any whitelistedIps.
  • scoping-workloads-in-vpc: Like vpc, but also requires security-group access via connectTo.
  • whitelisted-ips-only: Only from IP addresses listed in whitelistedIps.

  mongoDbAtlas:
    organizationId: 5f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e

      # [!code focus-end]

  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/index.ts
      joinDefaultVpc: true
      connectTo:
        - appDb

properties.longDescription: No effect in internet mode. In vpc/scoping-workloads-in-vpc, adds access for IPs outside the VPC. In whitelisted-ips-only, these are the only IPs that can connect.

resources:

properties.name: availabilityZones

• 1: Cheapest, but no redundancy if that AZ goes down.

Each NAT Gateway gets a static Elastic IP that persists across deployments — useful for IP whitelisting with external services.

properties.name: port
properties.shortDescription: Port this listener accepts traffic on.

resources:

properties.name: cdn
properties.shortDescription: CDN cache controls for SSR routes and specific path patterns.

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: customDomains
properties.shortDescription: Attach custom domains with auto-managed DNS records and TLS certificates.
properties.longDescription: Prerequisite: A Route 53 hosted zone for your domain must exist in your AWS account.

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: nextjs-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: ./
      # [!code focus-start]
      customDomains:
        - domainName: app.example.com
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: dev
properties.shortDescription: Dev server config for stacktape dev. Defaults to next dev.

properties.name: environment
properties.shortDescription: Environment variables for the SSR function. Use $ResourceParam() or $Secret() for dynamic values.

examples.code:
resources:
  database:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db.password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
          version: '16.6'
  web:
    type: nextjs-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: ./
      connectTo:
        - database
      # [!code focus-start]
      environment:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          value: $ResourceParam('database', 'connectionString')
        - name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
          value: $Secret('stripe.secretKey')
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: fileOptions
properties.shortDescription: Set custom headers (e.g., Cache-Control) for static files matching a pattern.

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: nextjs-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: ./
      # [!code focus-start]
      fileOptions:
        - includePattern: '**/*.{js,css,woff2}'
          headers:
            - key: Cache-Control
              value: 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: iamRoleStatements
properties.shortDescription: Raw IAM policy statements for permissions not covered by connectTo.
properties.longDescription: Added as a separate policy alongside auto-generated permissions. Use this for accessing AWS services directly (e.g., Rekognition, Textract, Bedrock).

examples.code:
resources:
  processor:
    type: batch-job
    properties:
      container:
        packaging:
          type: stacktape-image-buildpack
          properties:
            entryfilePath: src/job.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
      # [!code focus-start]
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - textract:AnalyzeDocument
          Resource:
            - '*'
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: serverLambda
properties.shortDescription: Customize the SSR Lambda function (memory, timeout, VPC, logging).

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: accessibilityMode
properties.shortDescription: How the domain can be reached.
properties.longDescription:
• internet: Accessible from anywhere (still requires IAM credentials).
  • vpc: Only accessible from resources inside your VPC (functions with joinDefaultVpc: true, containers, batch jobs).
  • scoping-workloads-in-vpc: Like vpc, but also requires security-group access via connectTo.

Cannot be changed after creation — switching between internet and VPC modes requires a new domain.

    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:

        instanceCount: 2
      storage:
        size: 50
      accessibility:
        # [!code focus-start]
        accessibilityMode: scoping-workloads-in-vpc
        # [!code focus-end]
  indexer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/indexer.ts

      connectTo:

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      # [!code focus-start]
      enableRemoteSessions: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: environment
properties.shortDescription: Environment variables injected into the container at runtime.
properties.longDescription: Use for configuration like API keys, feature flags, or secrets. Variables from connectTo (e.g., STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING) are added automatically.

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      # [!code focus-start]
      environment:
        - name: LOG_LEVEL
          value: info
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          value: $ResourceParam('mainDb', 'connectionString')
      # [!code focus-end]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro

properties.name: iamRoleStatements
properties.shortDescription: Raw IAM policy statements for permissions not covered by connectTo.
properties.longDescription: Added as a separate policy alongside auto-generated permissions. Use this for accessing AWS services directly (e.g., Rekognition, Textract, Bedrock).

examples.code:
resources:
  processor:
    type: batch-job
    properties:
      container:
        packaging:
          type: stacktape-image-buildpack
          properties:
            entryfilePath: src/job.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
      # [!code focus-start]
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - textract:AnalyzeDocument
          Resource:
            - '*'
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: internalHealthCheck
properties.shortDescription: Health check that auto-replaces unhealthy containers.
properties.longDescription: If a container fails the health check, it's terminated and replaced automatically.

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      # [!code focus-start]
      internalHealthCheck:
        healthCheckCommand:
          - CMD-SHELL
          - curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1
        intervalSeconds: 30
        retries: 3
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: loadBalancing
properties.shortDescription: How traffic reaches this service from other resources.
properties.longDescription:
• service-connect (default, ~$0.50/mo): Direct container-to-container. Cheapest option. Only reachable from other container-based resources in the stack.
  • application-load-balancer (~$18/mo): HTTP load balancer. Reachable from any VPC resource.

examples.code:
resources:
  paymentsService:
    type: private-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/payments.ts
      port: 3000
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      loadBalancing:
        type: application-load-balancer
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: logging
properties.shortDescription: Logging configuration.
properties.longDescription: Container output (stdout/stderr) is automatically sent to CloudWatch and retained for 90 days. View logs with stacktape logs or in the Stacktape Console.

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      # [!code focus-start]
      logging:
        retentionDays: 30
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: port
properties.shortDescription: Port this service listens on. Injected as the PORT env var.

examples.code:
resources:
  internalApi:

        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts

      port: 8080
      # [!code focus-end]
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 1024
      environment:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production

properties.name: protocol
properties.shortDescription: Protocol for metrics collection. Set to enable protocol-specific metrics (e.g., HTTP 5xx tracking).

examples.code:
resources:

      protocol: grpc
      # [!code focus-end]
      resources:
        cpu: 2
        memory: 2048

properties.name: scaling
properties.shortDescription: Auto-scaling: add/remove container instances based on demand.
properties.longDescription: Traffic is automatically distributed across all running containers.

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack

        memory: 1024

      scaling:
        minInstances: 2
        maxInstances: 10
        scalingPolicy:
          keepAvgCpuUtilizationUnder: 70
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: sideContainers
properties.shortDescription: Helper containers that run alongside the main container.
properties.longDescription:
• run-on-init: Runs to completion before the main container starts (e.g., database migrations).
  • always-running: Runs for the entire lifecycle (e.g., log forwarders, monitoring agents). Can reach the main container via localhost.

properties.name: stopTimeout
properties.shortDescription: Seconds to wait for graceful shutdown before force-killing the container.
properties.longDescription: The container receives SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL after this timeout. Must be 2-120.

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      # [!code focus-start]
      stopTimeout: 30
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT
properties.shortDescription: Deploy in private subnets with a static outbound IP via NAT Gateway.
properties.longDescription:
The container won't have a public IP. All outbound traffic routes through a NAT Gateway, giving you a static IP you can whitelist in external services (APIs, payment gateways, etc.).

Configure the number of NAT Gateways in stackConfig.vpc.nat.

Adds cost: NAT Gateway ~$32/month + data processing fees.

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      # [!code focus-start]
      usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: volumeMounts
properties.shortDescription: Persistent EFS volumes shared across containers and restarts.
properties.longDescription: Data stored in EFS volumes persists even when containers are replaced. Multiple containers can mount the same volume. All data is encrypted in transit.

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack

            mountPath: /data
      # [!code focus-end]
  sharedData:
    type: efs-filesystem
    properties: {}

properties.name: minify
properties.shortDescription: Minify Python code to reduce package size. Makes production stack traces harder to read.

examples.code:

properties.shortDescription: The Python package manager to use.
properties.longDescription: Stacktape uses uv for dependency resolution and installation. This option is kept for compatibility and must be set to uv if provided.

examples.code:

properties.name: runAppAs
properties.shortDescription: Python server type: WSGI (Flask, Django) or ASGI (FastAPI, Starlette).
properties.longDescription: Only for stacktape-image-buildpack. Auto-binds to the PORT env var. Set entryfilePath to module/file.py:app (e.g., app/main.py:app).

properties.name: uvOnlyGroups
properties.shortDescription: Only include these dependency groups from pyproject.toml.
properties.longDescription: Each value is passed to uv pip compile as --only-group <name>. This omits the project dependencies and default groups, matching uv behavior.

properties.name: limit
properties.shortDescription: Max requests per IP in a 5-minute window. Range: 100–20,000,000. Exceeding triggers the action.

examples.code:

            priority: 0
  apiService:

    properties:

        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/index.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      loadBalancing:
        type: application-load-balancer
      useFirewall: apiFirewall

properties.name: priority
properties.shortDescription: Evaluation order. Lower = evaluated first. Must be unique across all rules.

examples.code:

        memory: 512

        type: application-load-balancer
      useFirewall: apiFirewall

properties.name: action
properties.shortDescription: What to do when the rate limit is exceeded.
properties.longDescription:
• Block: Return 403 (most common for rate limiting).
  • Count: Log only, don't block (useful for testing thresholds).
  • Captcha/Challenge: Verify the client is human.

examples.code:

      useFirewall: apiFirewall

RdsEngine.shortDescription: Standard RDS: single-instance database with predictable pricing.

properties.name: instanceSize
properties.shortDescription: Instance size (e.g., db.t4g.micro, db.r6g.large).
properties.longDescription:
Determines CPU, memory, and network capacity. Quick guide:

  • db.t4g.micro (~$12/mo): Dev/testing, 2 vCPU, 1 GB RAM
  • db.t4g.medium (~$50/mo): Small production, 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM
  • db.r6g.large (~$180/mo): Production, 2 vCPU, 16 GB RAM

t family instances are burstable (fine for low/variable load). Use r family for steady workloads.

examples.code:
resources:
mainDatabase:
  type: relational-database
  properties:
    credentials:
      masterUserPassword: $Secret('mainDatabase.password')
    engine:
      type: postgres
      properties:
        version: '16.6'
        primaryInstance:
          # [!code focus-start]
          instanceSize: db.r6g.large
          # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: multiAz
properties.shortDescription: Create a standby replica in another availability zone for automatic failover.
properties.longDescription: If the primary goes down, traffic fails over to the standby automatically. Also reduces downtime during maintenance. Doubles the instance cost.

          multiAz: true
          # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: instanceSize
properties.shortDescription: The size of each Redis node. Affects memory, performance, and cost.
properties.longDescription:
Quick guide:

  • cache.t4g.micro (~$0.016/hr, 0.5 GB): Development, testing, low-traffic apps.
  • cache.t4g.small (~$0.032/hr, 1.37 GB): Small production apps, session stores.
  • cache.m7g.large (~$0.15/hr, 6.38 GB): Production workloads with moderate data.
  • cache.r7g.large (~$0.20/hr, 13.07 GB): Large datasets, memory-heavy caching.

Families: t = burstable (cheap, variable). m = general purpose. r = memory-optimized. Suffix g = ARM/Graviton (better price-performance).

This size applies to every node (primary + replicas). You can change it later without data loss.

properties.name: engine

properties.longDescription:
• RDS (postgres, mysql, mariadb, etc.): Single-node, fixed-size. Simple and predictable pricing.
  • Aurora (aurora-postgresql, aurora-mysql): High-performance clustered DB with auto-failover. Up to 5x faster than standard MySQL / 3x faster than standard PostgreSQL.
  • Aurora Serverless v2 (aurora-postgresql-serverless-v2): Auto-scales from 0.5 to 128 ACUs. Recommended for most new projects — pay only for what you use.

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: filterPolicy
properties.shortDescription: Filter messages by attributes so only relevant ones trigger the function.
properties.longDescription: Uses SNS subscription filter policy syntax. For content-based filtering, use EventBridge instead.

properties.name: onDeliveryFailure
properties.shortDescription: A destination for messages that fail to be delivered to the target.
properties.longDescription: In rare cases (e.g., if the target function cannot scale fast enough), a message might fail to be delivered. This property specifies an SQS queue where failed messages will be sent.

properties.name: snsTopicArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of an existing SNS topic.
properties.longDescription: Use this to subscribe to a topic that is not managed by your stack. You must specify either snsTopicName or snsTopicArn.

properties.name: snsTopicName
properties.shortDescription: The name of an SNS topic defined in your stack's resources.
properties.longDescription: You must specify either snsTopicName or snsTopicArn.

properties.name: sqsQueueArn
properties.shortDescription:
The ARN of the SQS queue for failed messages.

Specify exactly one of sqsQueueArn or sqsQueueName.

properties.name: sqsQueueName
properties.shortDescription:
The name of an SQS queue (defined in your Stacktape configuration) for failed messages.

Specify exactly one of sqsQueueArn or sqsQueueName.

SnsTopic.shortDescription: Pub/sub messaging: publish once, deliver to many subscribers (Lambda, SQS, email, SMS, HTTP).

properties.name: overrides
properties.shortDescription: Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.
properties.longDescription: Use dot-notation paths to override specific properties on any child resource. Find resource logical IDs with stacktape info:stack.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    # [!code focus-start]
    overrides:
      MainDbDatabaseInstance:
        Properties.StorageEncrypted: true
    # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: contentBasedDeduplication
properties.shortDescription: Automatically deduplicates messages based on content (SHA-256 hash) within a 5-minute window.
properties.longDescription: Saves you from generating a unique deduplication ID for each message. Requires fifoEnabled: true.

examples.code:
resources:
  auditTopic:
    type: sns-topic
    properties:
      fifoEnabled: true
      # [!code focus-start]
      contentBasedDeduplication: true
      # [!code focus-end]
  auditLogger:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/audit.ts
      events:
        - type: sns
          properties:
            snsTopicName: auditTopic

properties.name: fifoEnabled
properties.shortDescription: Guarantees message order and exactly-once delivery. Use for financial transactions, sequential workflows.
properties.longDescription: FIFO topics can only deliver to FIFO SQS queues (not email, SMS, or HTTP). Requires either contentBasedDeduplication: true or a unique MessageDeduplicationId per message.

examples.code:
resources:
  transactionsTopic:
    type: sns-topic
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      fifoEnabled: true
      # [!code focus-end]
      contentBasedDeduplication: true
  paymentsProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-payment.ts
      events:
        - type: sns
          properties:
            snsTopicName: transactionsTopic

properties.name: smsDisplayName
properties.shortDescription: Sender name shown on SMS messages sent to subscribers (e.g., "MyApp"). Max 11 characters.

examples.code:
resources:
  orderEventsTopic:
    type: sns-topic
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      smsDisplayName: ShopAlerts
      # [!code focus-end]
  orderNotifier:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/notify.ts
      events:
        - type: sns
          properties:
            snsTopicName: orderEventsTopic

properties.name: overrides
properties.shortDescription: Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.
properties.longDescription: Use dot-notation paths to override specific properties on any child resource. Find resource logical IDs with stacktape info:stack.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    # [!code focus-start]
    overrides:
      MainDbDatabaseInstance:
        Properties.StorageEncrypted: true
    # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: appDirectory
properties.shortDescription: Directory containing your app.config.ts. For monorepos, point to the SolidStart workspace.

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: solidstart-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      appDirectory: ./packages/web
      # [!code focus-end]
      environment:

properties.name: buildCommand

      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: cdn
properties.shortDescription: CDN cache controls for SSR routes and specific path patterns.

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: solidstart-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      cdn:
        disableInvalidationAfterDeploy: false
        defaultCachingOptions:
          minTTL: 0
          defaultTTL: 60
          maxTTL: 3600
        pathCachingOverrides:
          - path: /_server-islands/*
            cachingOptions:
              defaultTTL: 0
              maxTTL: 0
      # [!code focus-end]
      customDomains:
        - domainName: app.example.com

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: customDomains
properties.shortDescription: Attach custom domains with auto-managed DNS records and TLS certificates.
properties.longDescription: Prerequisite: A Route 53 hosted zone for your domain must exist in your AWS account.

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: solidstart-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      customDomains:
        - domainName: app.example.com
      # [!code focus-end]
      environment:
        - name: PUBLIC_API_URL
          value: https://api.example.com

properties.name: dev
properties.shortDescription: Dev server config for stacktape dev. Defaults to vinxi dev.

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: solidstart-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      dev:
        command: pnpm run dev
        workingDirectory: ./packages/web
      # [!code focus-end]
      environment:
        - name: PUBLIC_API_URL
          value: https://api.example.com

properties.name: environment
properties.shortDescription: Environment variables for the SSR function. Use $ResourceParam() or $Secret() for dynamic values.

examples.code:
resources:
  database:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.6'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
  web:
    type: solidstart-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      environment:
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          value: $ResourceParam('database', 'connectionString')
        - name: SESSION_SECRET
          value: $Secret('session-secret')
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: fileOptions
properties.shortDescription: Set custom headers (e.g., Cache-Control) for static files matching a pattern.

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: solidstart-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      fileOptions:
        - includePattern: '**/*.html'
          headers:
            - key: Cache-Control
              value: no-cache
        - includePattern: assets/**
          headers:
            - key: Cache-Control
              value: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: iamRoleStatements
properties.shortDescription: Raw IAM policy statements for permissions not covered by connectTo.
properties.longDescription: Added as a separate policy alongside auto-generated permissions. Use this for accessing AWS services directly (e.g., Rekognition, Textract, Bedrock).

examples.code:
resources:
  processor:
    type: batch-job
    properties:
      container:
        packaging:
          type: stacktape-image-buildpack
          properties:
            entryfilePath: src/job.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
      # [!code focus-start]
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - textract:AnalyzeDocument
          Resource:
            - '*'
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: serverLambda
properties.shortDescription: Customize the SSR Lambda function (memory, timeout, VPC, logging).

examples.code:
resources:
  web:
    type: solidstart-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      serverLambda:
        memory: 2048
        timeout: 20
        logging:
          retentionDays: 30
      # [!code focus-end]
      environment:
        - name: PUBLIC_API_URL
          value: https://api.example.com

properties.name: useFirewall
properties.shortDescription: Name of a web-app-firewall resource to protect this app. Firewall scope must be cdn.

examples.code:
resources:
  firewall:
    type: web-app-firewall
    properties:
      scope: cdn
  web:
    type: solidstart-web
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      useFirewall: firewall
      # [!code focus-end]
      customDomains:
        - domainName: app.example.com

SqsIntegration.shortDescription: Triggers a function when new messages are available in an SQS queue.

properties.name: batchSize
properties.shortDescription: The maximum number of records to process in a single batch.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 10,000.

properties.name: maxBatchWindowSeconds
properties.shortDescription: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait before invoking the function with a batch of records.
properties.longDescription: Maximum is 300 seconds. If not set, the function is invoked as soon as messages are available.

properties.name: sqsQueueArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of an existing SQS queue.
properties.longDescription: Use this to consume messages from a queue that is not managed by your stack. You must specify either sqsQueueName or sqsQueueArn.

properties.name: sqsQueueName
properties.shortDescription: The name of an SQS queue defined in your stack's resources.
properties.longDescription: You must specify either sqsQueueName or sqsQueueArn.

SqsQueue.shortDescription: Message queue for decoupling services. Producers send messages, consumers process them at their own pace.

properties.name: overrides
properties.shortDescription: Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.
properties.longDescription: Use dot-notation paths to override specific properties on any child resource. Find resource logical IDs with stacktape info:stack.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:

          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    # [!code focus-start]
    overrides:
      MainDbDatabaseInstance:
        Properties.StorageEncrypted: true
    # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: thresholdCount
properties.shortDescription: Fires when received message count crosses this threshold.
properties.longDescription: Default: fires if average messages received per period > thresholdCount. Customize with statistic and comparisonOperator.

examples.code:
resources:
  ingestionQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      alarms:
        - description: Ingestion backlog growing
          trigger:
            type: sqs-queue-received-messages-count
            properties:
              # [!code focus-start]

              # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: comparisonOperator
properties.shortDescription: How to compare the metric value against the threshold.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDatabase:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserName: admin
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')

        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
      alarms:
        - description: Database free memory dropped below threshold

            type: database-free-memory
            properties:
              thresholdMB: 512
              # [!code focus-start]
              comparisonOperator: LessThanThreshold
              # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: statistic
properties.shortDescription: How to aggregate metric values within each period: avg, sum, min, max, p90, p95, p99.

examples.code:
resources:
  worker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: ./src/worker.ts
      alarms:
        - description: 99th-percentile duration too high
          trigger:
            type: lambda-duration
            properties:

              # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: evaluation
properties.shortDescription: How long and how often to evaluate the metric before triggering.
