SqsQueueEventBusIntegration.shortDescription: Routes events from an EventBridge event bus to this queue when they match a specified pattern.

properties.name: properties
properties.shortDescription: Properties of the integration

examples.code:
resources:
  shipmentQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          # [!code focus-start]
          properties:
            useDefaultBus: true
            eventPattern:
              source:
                - logistics-service
              detail-type:
                - ShipmentDispatched
          # [!code focus-end]
  shipmentWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/shipment-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: shipmentQueue

properties.name: eventPattern
properties.shortDescription: A pattern to filter events from the event bus.
properties.longDescription: Only events that match this pattern will trigger the target. For details on the syntax, see the AWS EventBridge documentation on event patterns.

properties.name: eventBusArn
properties.shortDescription: The ARN of an existing event bus.
properties.longDescription: Use this to subscribe to an event bus that is not managed by your stack. You must specify only one of eventBusArn, eventBusName, or useDefaultBus.

properties.name: eventBusName
properties.shortDescription: The name of an event bus defined in your stack's resources.
properties.longDescription: You must specify only one of eventBusArn, eventBusName, or useDefaultBus.

properties.name: input
properties.shortDescription: A fixed JSON object to be passed as the event payload.

properties.name: inputPath
properties.shortDescription: A JSONPath expression to extract a portion of the event to pass to the target.
properties.longDescription: This is useful for forwarding only a specific part of the event payload. You can only use one of input, inputPath, or inputTransformer.

examples.code:
resources:
  orderEvents:
    type: event-bus
  orderProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-order.ts
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          properties:
            eventBusName: orderEvents
            eventPattern:
              source:
                - my.orders
            # [!code focus-start]
            inputPath: $.detail
            # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: inputTransformer
properties.shortDescription: Customizes the event payload sent to the target.
properties.longDescription: This allows you to extract values from the original event and use them to construct a new payload. You can only use one of input, inputPath, or inputTransformer.

examples.code:
resources:
  orderEvents:
    type: event-bus
  orderProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-order.ts
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          properties:
            eventBusName: orderEvents
            eventPattern:
              source:
                - my.orders
            # [!code focus-start]
            inputTransformer:
              inputPathsMap:
                instanceId: $.detail.instance-id
                instanceState: $.detail.state
              inputTemplate:
                message: Instance <instanceId> is now in state <instanceState>.
            # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: messageGroupId
properties.shortDescription: Message group ID for FIFO queues. Required when the target queue has fifoEnabled: true.
properties.longDescription: Messages in the same group are processed in strict order. Different groups can be processed in parallel.

examples.code:
resources:
  auditEventBus:
    type: event-bus
  auditQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      fifoEnabled: true
      contentBasedDeduplication: true
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          properties:
            eventBusName: auditEventBus
            eventPattern:
              detail-type:
                - UserAction
            # [!code focus-start]
            messageGroupId: audit-events
            # [!code focus-end]
  auditWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/audit-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: auditQueue

properties.name: onDeliveryFailure
properties.shortDescription: A destination for events that fail to be delivered to the target.
properties.longDescription: In rare cases, an event might fail to be delivered. This property specifies an SQS queue where failed events will be sent.

properties.name: useDefaultBus
properties.shortDescription: Uses the default AWS event bus.
properties.longDescription: You must specify only one of eventBusArn, eventBusName, or useDefaultBus.

properties.name: Action
properties.shortDescription: SQS actions to allow or deny. E.g., ["sqs:SendMessage"] or ["sqs:*"].

examples.code:
resources:
  ingestQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      policyStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Principal:
            Service: events.amazonaws.com
          # [!code focus-start]
          Action:
            - sqs:SendMessage
            - sqs:GetQueueAttributes
          # [!code focus-end]
  ingestWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/ingest-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: ingestQueue

properties.name: Effect
properties.shortDescription: Allow or Deny access for the specified actions and principal.

examples.code:
resources:
  restrictedQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      policyStatements:
        # [!code focus-start]
        - Effect: Deny
        # [!code focus-end]
          Principal: "*"
          Action:
            - sqs:DeleteQueue
  restrictedWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/restricted-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: restrictedQueue

properties.name: Principal
properties.shortDescription: Who gets access: AWS account ID, IAM ARN, or `"*"` for everyone. E.g., `{ "Service": "sns.amazonaws.com" }`.

properties.name: Condition
properties.shortDescription: Optional conditions for when this statement applies (e.g., restrict by source ARN or IP range).

properties.name: alarms
properties.shortDescription: Additional alarms associated with this resource.
properties.longDescription: These alarms will be merged with any alarms configured globally in the console.

examples.code:
resources:
  backlogQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      alarms:
        - trigger:
            type: sqs-queue-received-messages-count
            properties:
              thresholdCount: 1000
          notificationTargets:
            - type: slack
              properties:
                conversationId: C0123456789
                accessToken: $Secret('slack-token')
      # [!code focus-end]
  backlogWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/backlog-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: backlogQueue

properties.name: contentBasedDeduplication
properties.shortDescription: Automatically deduplicates messages based on their content (SHA-256 hash of the body).
properties.longDescription: Within the 5-minute deduplication window, identical messages are delivered only once. Saves you from having to generate a unique MessageDeduplicationId for each message. Requires fifoEnabled: true.

examples.code:
resources:
  orderEventsQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      fifoEnabled: true
      # [!code focus-start]
      contentBasedDeduplication: true
      # [!code focus-end]
      visibilityTimeoutSeconds: 90
  orderEventConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/order-event-consumer.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: orderEventsQueue

properties.name: delayMessagesSecond
properties.shortDescription: Delay (in seconds) before new messages become visible to consumers. Range: 0–900.
properties.longDescription: Useful for introducing a buffer, e.g., waiting for related data to be available before processing.

examples.code:
resources:
  emailQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      delayMessagesSecond: 30
      # [!code focus-end]
      visibilityTimeoutSeconds: 60
  emailWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/email-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: emailQueue

properties.name: disabledGlobalAlarms
properties.shortDescription: Disables globally configured alarms for this resource.
properties.longDescription: Provide a list of alarm names as configured in the console.

examples.code:
resources:
  lowPriorityQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      disabledGlobalAlarms:
        - sqs-queue-not-empty
      # [!code focus-end]
      messageRetentionPeriodSeconds: 86400
  lowPriorityWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/low-priority-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: lowPriorityQueue

properties.name: events
properties.shortDescription: A list of event sources that trigger message delivery to this queue.
properties.longDescription: Currently supports EventBridge event bus integration for delivering events directly to the queue.

examples.code:
resources:
  appEventBus:
    type: event-bus
  orderQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      events:
        - type: event-bus
          properties:
            eventBusName: appEventBus
            eventPattern:
              detail-type:
                - OrderPlaced
      # [!code focus-end]
  orderWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/order-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: orderQueue

properties.name: fifoEnabled
properties.shortDescription: Creates a FIFO queue that guarantees message order and exactly-once delivery.
properties.longDescription:
Use when processing order matters (e.g., financial transactions, sequential workflows). FIFO queues have lower throughput (~300 msg/s without batching, ~3,000 with) compared to standard queues.

Requires either contentBasedDeduplication: true or a MessageDeduplicationId on each message.

examples.code:
resources:
  transactionsQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      fifoEnabled: true
      # [!code focus-end]
      contentBasedDeduplication: true
      visibilityTimeoutSeconds: 60
  transactionProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/transaction-processor.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: transactionsQueue

properties.name: fifoHighThroughput
properties.shortDescription: Enables high-throughput mode for FIFO queues (up to ~70,000 msg/s per queue).
properties.longDescription: Messages are partitioned by MessageGroupId — order is guaranteed within each group but not across groups. Requires fifoEnabled: true.

examples.code:
resources:
  clickstreamQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      fifoEnabled: true
      # [!code focus-start]
      fifoHighThroughput: true
      # [!code focus-end]
      contentBasedDeduplication: true
  clickstreamConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/clickstream-consumer.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: clickstreamQueue
            batchSize: 10

properties.name: longPollingSeconds
properties.shortDescription: Seconds the queue waits for messages before returning an empty response. Range: 0–20.
properties.longDescription:
Set to 1–20 to enable long polling, which reduces costs by making fewer API calls. With short polling (0), the consumer gets an immediate (often empty) response and must poll again.

Recommended: 20 for most workloads — it's the most cost-effective.

examples.code:
resources:
  imageJobsQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      longPollingSeconds: 20
      # [!code focus-end]
      visibilityTimeoutSeconds: 120
  imageWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/image-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: imageJobsQueue

properties.name: maxMessageSizeBytes
properties.shortDescription: Maximum message size in bytes. Range: 1,024 (1 KB) to 262,144 (256 KB).
properties.longDescription: Messages larger than this limit are rejected. For payloads over 256 KB, store the data in S3 and send the reference.

examples.code:
resources:
  uploadEventsQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      maxMessageSizeBytes: 65536
      # [!code focus-end]
      messageRetentionPeriodSeconds: 604800
  uploadProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/upload-processor.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: uploadEventsQueue

properties.name: messageRetentionPeriodSeconds
properties.shortDescription: How long unprocessed messages stay in the queue before being deleted. Range: 60s to 1,209,600s (14 days).
properties.longDescription: Default is 4 days (345,600s). Increase if consumers might fall behind or be temporarily offline.

examples.code:
resources:
  reportJobsQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      messageRetentionPeriodSeconds: 1209600
      # [!code focus-end]
      visibilityTimeoutSeconds: 300
  reportWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/report-worker.ts
      timeout: 240
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: reportJobsQueue

properties.name: policyStatements
properties.shortDescription: Custom access-control statements added to the queue's resource policy.
properties.longDescription: These are merged with policies Stacktape auto-generates. Use to grant cross-account access or allow specific AWS services (e.g., SNS) to send messages to this queue.

examples.code:
resources:
  crossAccountQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      policyStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Principal:
            Service: sns.amazonaws.com
          Action:
            - sqs:SendMessage
      # [!code focus-end]
  crossAccountWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/cross-account-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: crossAccountQueue

properties.name: redrivePolicy
properties.shortDescription: Moves messages that fail processing too many times to a dead-letter queue for inspection.
properties.longDescription: After maxReceiveCount failed attempts, the message is automatically moved to a separate queue so you can investigate and reprocess it. Prevents poison messages from blocking the queue.

examples.code:
resources:
  paymentsDlq:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      messageRetentionPeriodSeconds: 1209600
  paymentsQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      redrivePolicy:
        targetSqsQueueName: paymentsDlq
        maxReceiveCount: 5
      # [!code focus-end]
      visibilityTimeoutSeconds: 60
  paymentsWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/payments-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: paymentsQueue

properties.name: visibilityTimeoutSeconds
properties.shortDescription: How long (seconds) a message is hidden from other consumers after being received. Range: 0–43,200 (12 hours).
properties.longDescription:
After a consumer picks up a message, it must delete it before this timeout expires — otherwise it becomes visible again and can be processed by another consumer (duplicate processing).

Set this higher than your expected processing time. If your tasks take 2 minutes, use at least 150 seconds.

examples.code:
resources:
  videoEncodeQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      visibilityTimeoutSeconds: 900
      # [!code focus-end]
      longPollingSeconds: 20
  videoEncoder:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/video-encoder.ts
      timeout: 600
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: videoEncodeQueue

properties.name: thresholdCount
properties.shortDescription: Fires when received message count crosses this threshold.
properties.longDescription: Default: fires if average messages received per period > thresholdCount. Customize with statistic and comparisonOperator.

examples.code:
resources:
  ingestionQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      alarms:
        - description: Ingestion backlog growing
          trigger:
            type: sqs-queue-received-messages-count
            properties:
              # [!code focus-start]
              thresholdCount: 5000
              # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: comparisonOperator
properties.shortDescription: How to compare the metric value against the threshold.

examples.code:
resources:
  mainDatabase:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserName: admin
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
      alarms:
        - description: Database free memory dropped below threshold
          trigger:
            type: database-free-memory
            properties:
              thresholdMB: 512
              # [!code focus-start]
              comparisonOperator: LessThanThreshold
              # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: statistic
properties.shortDescription: How to aggregate metric values within each period: avg, sum, min, max, p90, p95, p99.

examples.code:
resources:
  worker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: ./src/worker.ts
      alarms:
        - description: 99th-percentile duration too high
          trigger:
            type: lambda-duration
            properties:
              thresholdMilliseconds: 3000
              # [!code focus-start]
              statistic: p99
              # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: maxReceiveCount
properties.shortDescription: How many times a message can be received (and fail) before being moved to the dead-letter queue.
properties.longDescription: A typical starting value is 3–5. Set lower for fast-failing workloads, higher for retryable transient errors.

examples.code:
resources:
  jobsDlq:
    type: sqs-queue
  jobsQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      redrivePolicy:
        targetSqsQueueName: jobsDlq
        # [!code focus-start]
        maxReceiveCount: 3
        # [!code focus-end]
  jobsWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/jobs-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: jobsQueue

properties.name: targetSqsQueueArn
properties.shortDescription: ARN of an external SQS queue to use as the dead-letter queue. Use when the DLQ is in another stack or account.

examples.code:
resources:
  eventsQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      redrivePolicy:
        # [!code focus-start]
        targetSqsQueueArn: arn:aws:sqs:eu-west-1:123456789012:shared-dead-letter-queue
        # [!code focus-end]
        maxReceiveCount: 4
  eventsWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/events-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: eventsQueue

properties.name: targetSqsQueueName
properties.shortDescription: Name of another sqs-queue in your config to use as the dead-letter queue.

examples.code:
resources:
  notificationsDlq:
    type: sqs-queue
  notificationsQueue:
    type: sqs-queue
    properties:
      redrivePolicy:
        # [!code focus-start]
        targetSqsQueueName: notificationsDlq
        # [!code focus-end]
        maxReceiveCount: 3
  notificationsWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/notifications-worker.ts
      events:
        - type: sqs
          properties:
            sqsQueueName: notificationsQueue

SsrWebCdnConfig.shortDescription: CDN configuration shared by all SSR web resources

properties.name: defaultCachingOptions
properties.shortDescription: Override default SSR caching behavior for all routes handled by the server.
properties.longDescription: Useful when you want to cache SSR responses longer than the framework defaults.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      cdn:
        # [!code focus-start]
        defaultCachingOptions:
          minTTL: 0
          defaultTTL: 60
          maxTTL: 3600
          cacheKeyParameters:
            queryString:
              all: true
            cookies:
              none: true
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: disableInvalidationAfterDeploy
properties.shortDescription: Skip clearing the CDN cache after each deploy.
properties.longDescription: By default, all cached content is flushed on every deploy so users see the latest version. Set to true if you manage cache invalidation yourself or want to keep cached content between deploys.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      cdn:
        # [!code focus-start]
        disableInvalidationAfterDeploy: true
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: pathCachingOverrides
properties.shortDescription: Override caching for specific CDN path patterns.
properties.longDescription: Matches existing framework-managed paths (e.g. _astro/*, _next/data/*) or adds new server-path caching rules (e.g. /_server-islands/*) while preserving managed routing.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      cdn:
        # [!code focus-start]
        pathCachingOverrides:
          - path: /_server-islands/*
            cachingOptions:
              minTTL: 0
              defaultTTL: 0
              maxTTL: 0
          - path: /api/*
            cachingOptions:
              cacheMethods:
                - GET
                - HEAD
                - OPTIONS
              defaultTTL: 30
        # [!code focus-end]

SsrWebDevConfig.shortDescription: Dev server configuration shared by all SSR web resources

properties.name: command
properties.shortDescription: Override the default dev server command (e.g., npm run dev).

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      dev:
        # [!code focus-start]
        command: npm run dev
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: workingDirectory
properties.shortDescription: Working directory for the dev command, relative to project root.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: packages/web
      dev:
        command: npm run dev
        # [!code focus-start]
        workingDirectory: packages/web
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: cachingOptions
properties.shortDescription: Caching behavior override for this path pattern.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      cdn:
        pathCachingOverrides:
          - path: /api/*
            # [!code focus-start]
            cachingOptions:
              cacheMethods:
                - GET
                - HEAD
              minTTL: 0
              defaultTTL: 15
              maxTTL: 300
              cacheKeyParameters:
                queryString:
                  whitelist:
                    - page
                    - limit
            # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: path
properties.shortDescription: URL path pattern to match (e.g., /api/*, /_server-islands/*).

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      cdn:
        pathCachingOverrides:
          # [!code focus-start]
          -
            path: /_nuxt/*
          # [!code focus-end]
            cachingOptions:
              minTTL: 31536000
              defaultTTL: 31536000
              maxTTL: 31536000

SsrWebServerLambdaConfig.shortDescription: Server Lambda configuration shared by all SSR web resources

properties.name: joinDefaultVpc
properties.shortDescription: Connect to VPC resources (databases, Redis). Warning: function loses direct internet access.

examples.code:
resources:
  database:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('database.password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.6'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
      accessibility:
        accessibilityMode: scoping-workloads-in-vpc
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      connectTo:
        - database
      environment:
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          value: $ResourceParam('database', 'connectionString')
      serverLambda:
        memory: 1024
        # [!code focus-start]
        joinDefaultVpc: true
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: logging
properties.shortDescription: Logging config. Logs are sent to CloudWatch. View with stacktape logs or in the AWS console.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      serverLambda:
        memory: 1024
        # [!code focus-start]
        logging:
          retentionDays: 30
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: memory
properties.shortDescription: Memory in MB (128–10,240). CPU scales proportionally — 1,769 MB = 1 vCPU.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      environment:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
      serverLambda:
        # [!code focus-start]
        memory: 2048
        # [!code focus-end]
        timeout: 20

properties.name: timeout
properties.shortDescription: Max execution time in seconds. Max: 30.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApp:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: .
      serverLambda:
        memory: 1024
        # [!code focus-start]
        timeout: 25
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: disableStackInfoSaving
properties.shortDescription: Stop saving stack info to a local file after each deployment.
properties.longDescription: By default, Stacktape saves resource details and custom outputs to .stacktape-stack-info/{stackName}.json after every deploy.

examples.code:
stackConfig:
  # [!code focus-start]
  disableStackInfoSaving: true
  # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512

properties.name: outputs
properties.shortDescription: Custom values to display and save after each deployment.
properties.longDescription:
Use outputs to surface dynamic values like API URLs, database endpoints, or resource ARNs that are only known after deployment. Outputs are:

  • Printed in the terminal after deploy
  • Saved to the stack info JSON file
  • Optionally exported for cross-stack references (via export: true)

examples.code:
stackConfig:
  # [!code focus-start]
  outputs:
    - name: ApiUrl
      value: $ResourceParam('api', 'url')
  # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512

properties.name: stackInfoDirectory
properties.shortDescription: Directory for the stack info JSON file.
properties.longDescription: Relative to the project root.

examples.code:
stackConfig:
  # [!code focus-start]
  stackInfoDirectory: ./build/stack-info
  # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512

properties.name: tags
properties.shortDescription: Tags applied to every AWS resource in this stack.
properties.longDescription:
Useful for cost tracking, access control, and organization. Stacktape automatically adds projectName, stage, and stackName tags — your custom tags are merged on top.

Max 45 tags.

examples.code:
stackConfig:
  # [!code focus-start]
  tags:
    - name: team
      value: payments
    - name: costCenter
      value: '4100'
  # [!code focus-end]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:

StateMachine.shortDescription: Visual workflow engine for orchestrating Lambda functions, API calls, and other AWS services.

properties.name: overrides
properties.shortDescription: Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.
properties.longDescription: Use dot-notation paths to override specific properties on any child resource. Find resource logical IDs with stacktape info:stack.

examples.code:

          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro

properties.name: StartAt
properties.shortDescription: The name of the state to start the execution at.

examples.code:

    properties:
      definition:
        Comment: Validate incoming data before processing
        # [!code focus-start]
        StartAt: ValidateInput
        # [!code focus-end]
        States:
          ValidateInput:
            Type: Task
            Resource:
              Fn::GetAtt:
                - ValidateInputFunction
                - Arn
            End: true

properties.name: States
properties.shortDescription: An object containing the states of the state machine.

examples.code:

        # [!code focus-start]
        States:
          Extract:
            Type: Task
            Resource:
              Fn::GetAtt:
                - ExtractFunction
                - Arn
            Next: Transform
          Transform:
            Type: Task
            Resource:
              Fn::GetAtt:
                - TransformFunction
                - Arn
            End: true

properties.name: Resource
properties.shortDescription: ARNs of the AWS resources this statement applies to. Use "*" for all resources.

examples.code:

    type: web-service

            - rekognition:DetectText
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: Action
properties.shortDescription: AWS actions to allow or deny (e.g., s3:GetObject, sqs:SendMessage).

properties.name: Condition
properties.shortDescription: Conditions under which this statement applies (e.g., IP restrictions, tag-based access).
properties.longDescription:
**Example (YAML):**

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - s3:GetObject
          Resource:
            - 'arn:aws:s3:::my-secure-bucket/*'
          Condition:
            Bool:
              'aws:SecureTransport': 'true'
```

**Example (TypeScript):**

```ts
import { WebService, StacktapeImageBuildpackPackaging, defineConfig } from 'stacktape';

export default defineConfig(() => {
  const api = new WebService({
    packaging: new StacktapeImageBuildpackPackaging({ entryfilePath: 'src/server.ts' }),
    resources: { cpu: 0.25, memory: 512 },
    iamRoleStatements: [
      {
        Effect: 'Allow',
        Action: ['s3:GetObject'],
        Resource: ['arn:aws:s3:::my-secure-bucket/*'],
        Condition: { Bool: { 'aws:SecureTransport': 'true' } }
      }
    ]
  });

  return { resources: { api } };
});
```

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: iamRoleStatements

    type: batch-job
    properties:

        packaging:
          type: stacktape-image-buildpack
          properties:

      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
      # [!code focus-start]

        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - textract:AnalyzeDocument
          Resource:
            - '*'
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.shortDescription: Customize the SSR Lambda function (memory, timeout, VPC, logging).

properties.name: accessTokenValiditySeconds
properties.shortDescription: Access token lifetime
properties.longDescription:
Controls how long an access token issued by Cognito stays valid after login. Shorter lifetimes reduce the window in which a stolen token can be abused, at the cost of more frequent refreshes.

This value is passed to the user pool client as AccessTokenValidity.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      accessTokenValiditySeconds: 3600
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: allowEmailAsUserName
properties.shortDescription: Allow email addresses as usernames
properties.longDescription:
If enabled (the default), users can sign in using their email address instead of a dedicated username. Turning this off means emails can still be stored, but can't be used to log in directly.

This is also controlled through Cognito UsernameAttributes.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      allowEmailAsUserName: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: allowOnlyAdminsToCreateAccount
properties.shortDescription: Restrict account creation to administrators
properties.longDescription:
If enabled, new users can't sign up themselves. Accounts must be created through an admin flow (for example from an internal admin tool or script), which helps prevent unwanted self-registrations.

Internally this controls AdminCreateUserConfig.AllowAdminCreateUserOnly on the Cognito user pool (AWS::Cognito::UserPool).

examples.code:
resources:
  adminPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      allowOnlyAdminsToCreateAccount: true
      # [!code focus-end]
      inviteMessageConfig:
        emailSubject: Your new account
        emailMessage: 'Your username is {username} and temporary password is {####}.'

properties.name: allowOnlyExternalIdentityProviders
properties.shortDescription: Force external identity providers
properties.longDescription:
If true, users can't sign in with a username/password against the Cognito user directory at all. Instead, they must always use one of the configured external identity providers (Google, SAML, etc.).

Internally this removes COGNITO from SupportedIdentityProviders on the user pool client.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
        - email
      identityProviders:
        - type: Google
          clientId: my-google-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
          clientSecret: $Secret('google-oauth.client-secret')
      # [!code focus-start]
      allowOnlyExternalIdentityProviders: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: allowPhoneNumberAsUserName
properties.shortDescription: Allow phone numbers as usernames
properties.longDescription:
If enabled (the default), users can sign in using their phone number in addition to any traditional username. Turning this off means phone numbers can still be stored, but can't be used to log in.

This is implemented via Cognito's UsernameAttributes configuration.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      allowPhoneNumberAsUserName: false
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: allowedOAuthFlows
properties.shortDescription: OAuth flows
properties.longDescription:
Specifies which OAuth 2.0 flows the user pool client is allowed to use:

  • code: Authorization Code flow (recommended for web apps and backends).
  • implicit: Implicit flow (legacy browser-only flow).
  • client_credentials: Server‑to‑server (no end user) machine credentials.

These values populate AllowedOAuthFlows on the Cognito user pool client (AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient).

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
        - email
      # [!code focus-start]
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: allowedOAuthScopes
properties.shortDescription: OAuth scopes
properties.longDescription:
Lists which scopes clients can request when using OAuth (for example email, openid, profile). Scopes control which user information and permissions your app receives in tokens.

These values are passed to the user pool client as AllowedOAuthScopes.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      # [!code focus-start]
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
        - email
        - profile
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: callbackURLs
properties.shortDescription: OAuth callback URLs
properties.longDescription:
The allowed URLs where Cognito is permitted to redirect users after successful authentication. These must exactly match the URLs registered with your frontend / backend, otherwise the redirect will fail.

Mapped into CallbackURLs and DefaultRedirectURI on the user pool client.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      # [!code focus-start]
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
        - http://localhost:3000/callback
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: customDomain
properties.shortDescription: Custom Domain
properties.longDescription:
Configures a custom domain for the Cognito Hosted UI (e.g., auth.example.com).

When configured, Cognito creates a CloudFront distribution to serve your custom domain. Stacktape automatically:

  • Configures the user pool domain with your custom domain and an ACM certificate from us-east-1
  • Creates a DNS record pointing to the CloudFront distribution

The domain must be registered and verified in your Stacktape account with a valid ACM certificate in us-east-1.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      # [!code focus-start]
      customDomain:
        domainName: auth.example.com
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: emailConfiguration
properties.shortDescription: Email delivery settings
properties.longDescription:
Controls how Cognito sends emails (verification messages, password reset codes, admin invitations, etc.). You can either use Cognito's built-in email service or plug in your own SES identity for full control over the sender.

This config is used to build the Cognito EmailConfiguration block (AWS docs).

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      emailConfiguration:
        sesAddressArn: arn:aws:ses:eu-west-1:123456789012:identity/example.com
        from: no-reply@example.com
        replyToEmailAddress: support@example.com
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: enableHostedUi
properties.shortDescription: Enable the Cognito Hosted UI
properties.longDescription: Turns on Cognito's Hosted UI – a pre-built, hosted login and registration page – so you don't have to build your own auth screens. This is useful when you want to get started quickly or keep authentication logic outside of your main app.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      enableHostedUi: true
      # [!code focus-end]
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: my-company-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      logoutURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/logout
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
        - email

properties.name: generateClientSecret
properties.shortDescription: Generate a client secret
properties.longDescription:
Asks Cognito to generate a secret for the user pool client. Use this when you have trusted backends (like APIs or server‑side apps) that can safely store a client secret and use confidential OAuth flows.

This flag controls the GenerateSecret property on the user pool client.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      generateClientSecret: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: hooks
properties.shortDescription: Lambda triggers for the user pool
properties.longDescription:
Connects AWS Lambda functions to Cognito "hooks" (triggers) such as pre-sign-up, post-confirmation, or token generation. You can use these to enforce additional validation, enrich user profiles, migrate users from another system, and more.

Internally this maps to the Cognito user pool LambdaConfig.

examples.code:
resources:
  postConfirmFn:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/post-confirmation.ts
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      hooks:
        postConfirmation: $ResourceParam('postConfirmFn', 'arn')
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: hostedUiCSS
properties.shortDescription: Custom CSS for the Hosted UI
properties.longDescription:
Lets you override the default Cognito Hosted UI styling with your own CSS (colors, fonts, layouts, etc.), so the login experience matches the rest of your application.

Behind the scenes this is applied using the AWS::Cognito::UserPoolUICustomizationAttachment resource.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: my-company-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      # [!code focus-start]
      hostedUiCSS: |
        .label-customizable { font-weight: 600; }
        .submitButton-customizable { background: #4f46e5; }
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: hostedUiDomainPrefix
properties.shortDescription: Hosted UI domain prefix
properties.longDescription: Sets the first part of your Hosted UI URL: https://<prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com. Pick something that matches your project or company name.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      # [!code focus-start]
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: my-company-auth
      # [!code focus-end]
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid

properties.name: idTokenValiditySeconds
properties.shortDescription: ID token lifetime
properties.longDescription:
Controls how long an ID token (which contains user profile and claims) is accepted before clients must obtain a new one.

This is set on the user pool client as IdTokenValidity.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      idTokenValiditySeconds: 3600
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: identityProviders
properties.shortDescription: External identity providers
properties.longDescription:
Allows users to sign in with third‑party identity providers like Google, Facebook, Login with Amazon, OIDC, SAML, or Sign in with Apple. Each entry configures one external provider (client ID/secret, attribute mapping, requested scopes, and advanced provider‑specific options).

Under the hood Stacktape creates separate AWS::Cognito::UserPoolIdentityProvider resources and registers them in the user pool client's SupportedIdentityProviders.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
        - email
      # [!code focus-start]
      identityProviders:
        - type: Google
          clientId: my-google-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
          clientSecret: $Secret('google-oauth.client-secret')
          authorizeScopes:
            - openid
            - email
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: inviteMessageConfig
properties.shortDescription: Invite message overrides
properties.longDescription:
Customizes the contents of the "invitation" message that users receive when an administrator creates their account (for example, when sending a temporary password and sign-in instructions).

If you want to send custom emails through SES, you must also configure emailConfiguration.sesAddressArn.

examples.code:
resources:
  adminPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      allowOnlyAdminsToCreateAccount: true
      # [!code focus-start]
      inviteMessageConfig:
        emailSubject: Welcome to Acme
        emailMessage: 'Hi {username}, your temporary password is {####}.'
        smsMessage: 'Acme login: {username} / {####}'
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: logoutURLs
properties.shortDescription: OAuth logout URLs
properties.longDescription:
The URLs Cognito can redirect users to after they log out of the Hosted UI or end their session. Must also be explicitly configured so that sign-out redirects don't fail.

These populate the LogoutURLs list on the user pool client.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      # [!code focus-start]
      logoutURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/logout
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: mfaConfiguration
properties.shortDescription: Multi-factor authentication
properties.longDescription:
Controls whether you use Multi‑Factor Authentication (MFA) and which second factors are allowed. MFA makes it much harder for attackers to access accounts even if they know a user's password.

Under the hood this config drives both the MfaConfiguration and EnabledMfas properties in Cognito (see "MFA configuration" in the AWS::Cognito::UserPool docs).

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      mfaConfiguration:
        status: OPTIONAL
        enabledTypes:
          - SOFTWARE_TOKEN
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: passwordPolicy
properties.shortDescription: Password strength rules
properties.longDescription:
Defines how strong user passwords must be – minimum length and whether they must include lowercase, uppercase, numbers, and/or symbols – plus how long temporary passwords issued to new users remain valid.

This is applied to the Cognito Policies.PasswordPolicy block.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      passwordPolicy:
        minimumLength: 12
        requireLowercase: true
        requireUppercase: true
        requireNumbers: true
        requireSymbols: true
        temporaryPasswordValidityDays: 7
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: refreshTokenValidityDays
properties.shortDescription: Refresh token lifetime
properties.longDescription:
Sets for how many days a refresh token can be used to obtain new access / ID tokens without requiring the user to sign in again. Longer lifetimes mean fewer re-authentications, but keep sessions alive for longer.

This value is used as RefreshTokenValidity on the Cognito user pool client.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      refreshTokenValidityDays: 30
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: requireEmailVerification
properties.shortDescription: (Reserved) Require verified emails
properties.longDescription:
Present for forward compatibility. Stacktape currently derives email / phone verification behavior from userVerificationType, not from this flag directly.

To require email-based verification today, use userVerificationType: 'email-link' | 'email-code' instead.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      requireEmailVerification: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: requirePhoneNumberVerification
properties.shortDescription: (Reserved) Require verified phone numbers
properties.longDescription:
Present for forward compatibility. Stacktape currently derives email / phone verification behavior from userVerificationType, not from this flag directly.

To require SMS-based verification today, use userVerificationType: 'sms'.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: sms
      # [!code focus-start]
      requirePhoneNumberVerification: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: schema
properties.shortDescription: Custom attributes schema
properties.longDescription:
Lets you define additional attributes (like role, plan, companyId, etc.) that are stored on each user, including their data type and validation constraints.

These translate into the Cognito user pool Schema entries (schema docs).

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      schema:
        - name: plan
          attributeDataType: String
          mutable: true
          stringMinLength: 1
          stringMaxLength: 32
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: unusedAccountValidityDays
properties.shortDescription: Expire unused admin-created accounts
properties.longDescription:
When an admin creates a user account, Cognito issues a temporary password. This setting controls how many days that temporary password (and the corresponding account) stays valid if the user never signs in.

Internally this maps to AdminCreateUserConfig.UnusedAccountValidityDays.

examples.code:
resources:
  adminPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      allowOnlyAdminsToCreateAccount: true
      # [!code focus-start]
      unusedAccountValidityDays: 7
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: useFirewall
properties.shortDescription: Associate a WAF
properties.longDescription:
Links the user pool to a web-app-firewall resource, so requests to the Hosted UI and token endpoints are inspected by AWS WAF rules you configure in Stacktape.

Stacktape does this by creating a WebACLAssociation between the user pool and the referenced firewall.

examples.code:
resources:
  authFirewall:
    type: web-app-firewall
    properties:
      scope: regional
      rules:
        - type: managed-rule-group
          properties:
            name: AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet
            vendorName: AWS
            priority: 10
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      # [!code focus-start]
      useFirewall: authFirewall
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: userVerificationMessageConfig
properties.shortDescription: Verification message text
properties.longDescription: Lets you customize the exact email and SMS texts that Cognito sends when asking users to verify their email / phone. For example, you can change subjects, body text, or the message that contains the {} verification code.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      # [!code focus-start]
      userVerificationMessageConfig:
        emailSubjectUsingCode: Verify your Acme account
        emailMessageUsingCode: 'Your verification code is {####}.'
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: userVerificationType
properties.shortDescription: Verification strategy
properties.longDescription:
Chooses how new users prove that they own their contact information:

  • email-link: Cognito emails a clickable link.
  • email-code: Cognito emails a short numeric code.
  • sms: Cognito sends a code via SMS to the user's phone number.
  • none: Users aren't required to verify email or phone during sign-up.

Stacktape uses this value to configure AutoVerifiedAttributes and VerificationMessageTemplate on the underlying Cognito user pool.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      # [!code focus-start]
      userVerificationType: email-link
      # [!code focus-end]
      allowEmailAsUserName: true

properties.name: domainName
properties.shortDescription: Domain Name
properties.longDescription: Fully qualified domain name for the Cognito Hosted UI (e.g., auth.example.com).

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      customDomain:
        # [!code focus-start]
        domainName: auth.example.com
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: customCertificateArn
properties.shortDescription: Custom Certificate ARN
properties.longDescription:
ARN of an ACM certificate in us-east-1 to use for this domain. By default, Stacktape uses the certificate associated with your domain in us-east-1.

The certificate must be in us-east-1 because Cognito uses CloudFront for custom domains.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      customDomain:
        domainName: auth.example.com
        # [!code focus-start]
        customCertificateArn: arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:123456789012:certificate/abcd1234-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: disableDnsRecordCreation
properties.shortDescription: Disable DNS Record Creation
properties.longDescription: If true, Stacktape will not create a DNS record for this domain.

examples.code:
resources:
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      enableHostedUi: true
      hostedUiDomainPrefix: acme-auth
      callbackURLs:
        - https://app.example.com/callback
      allowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      allowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
      customDomain:
        domainName: auth.example.com
        # [!code focus-start]
        disableDnsRecordCreation: true
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: createAuthChallenge
properties.shortDescription:
Create auth challenge hook

Part of Cognito's custom auth flow. This trigger is used to generate a challenge (for example sending a custom OTP) after DefineAuthChallenge decides a challenge is needed.

examples.code:
resources:
  createAuthChallengeFn:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/create-auth-challenge.ts
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      hooks:
        # [!code focus-start]
        createAuthChallenge: $ResourceParam('createAuthChallengeFn', 'arn')
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: customMessage
properties.shortDescription:
Custom message hook

Triggered whenever Cognito is about to send an email or SMS (sign‑up, verification, password reset, etc.). Lets you fully customize message contents or dynamically choose language/branding.

Value must be the ARN of a Lambda function configured to handle the "Custom Message" trigger.

examples.code:
resources:
  customMessageFn:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/custom-message.ts
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      hooks:
        # [!code focus-start]
        customMessage: $ResourceParam('customMessageFn', 'arn')
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: defineAuthChallenge
properties.shortDescription:
Define auth challenge hook

Also part of the custom auth flow. It decides whether a user needs another challenge, has passed, or has failed, based on previous challenges and responses.

examples.code:
resources:
  defineAuthChallengeFn:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/define-auth-challenge.ts
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      hooks:
        # [!code focus-start]
        defineAuthChallenge: $ResourceParam('defineAuthChallengeFn', 'arn')
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: postAuthentication
properties.shortDescription:
Post-authentication hook

Runs after a user has successfully authenticated. You can use this to record analytics, update last‑login timestamps, or block access based on additional checks.

examples.code:
resources:
  postAuthenticationFn:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/post-authentication.ts
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      hooks:
        # [!code focus-start]
        postAuthentication: $ResourceParam('postAuthenticationFn', 'arn')
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: postConfirmation
properties.shortDescription:
Post-confirmation hook

Runs right after a user confirms their account (for example via email link or admin confirmation). This is often used to create user records in your own database or to provision resources.

examples.code:
resources:
  postConfirmationFn:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/post-confirmation.ts
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      hooks:
        # [!code focus-start]
        postConfirmation: $ResourceParam('postConfirmationFn', 'arn')
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: preAuthentication
properties.shortDescription:
Pre-authentication hook

Invoked just before Cognito validates a user's credentials. You can use this to block sign‑in attempts based on IP, device, or user state (for example, soft‑deleting an account).

examples.code:
resources:
  preAuthenticationFn:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/pre-authentication.ts
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      hooks:
        # [!code focus-start]
        preAuthentication: $ResourceParam('preAuthenticationFn', 'arn')
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: preSignUp
properties.shortDescription:
Pre-sign-up hook

Called before a new user is created. Useful for validating input, auto‑confirming trusted users, or blocking sign‑ups that don't meet your business rules.

examples.code:
resources:
  preSignUpFn:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-lambda-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/pre-sign-up.ts
  userPool:
    type: user-auth-pool
    properties:
      userVerificationType: email-code
      hooks:
        # [!code focus-start]
        preSignUp: $ResourceParam('preSignUpFn', 'arn')
        # [!code focus-end]

properties.shortDescription:
Emit TypeScript decorator metadata. Required by NestJS, TypeORM, and similar frameworks.

Source maps are disabled for this artifact because the decorator transform and bundler cannot yet compose their mappings accurately. Emitting a map would give production stack traces incorrect line numbers.

properties.shortDescription: A list of dependencies to exclude from the main bundle.
properties.longDescription: These dependencies will be treated as "external" and will not be bundled directly into your application's code. Instead, they will be installed separately in the deployment package. Use * to exclude all dependencies from the bundle.

     memory: 1024

properties.shortDescription: Output module format: cjs (CommonJS) or esm (ES Modules, enables top-level await).

properties.shortDescription: Alarms for this service (merged with global alarms from the Stacktape Console).

properties.name: metric
properties.shortDescription: The metric to monitor on the Load Balancer.
properties.longDescription:
The threshold will be compared against the calculated value of statistic(METRIC), where:

  • statistic is the function applied to the metric values collected during the evaluation period (default: avg).
  • METRIC is the chosen metric.

Available Metrics:

  • ActiveConnectionCount: The total number of concurrent TCP connections active from clients to the load balancer and from the load balancer to targets.
  • AnomalousHostCount: The number of hosts detected with anomalies.
  • ClientTLSNegotiationErrorCount: The number of TLS connections initiated by the client that did not establish a session with the load balancer due to a TLS error.
  • ConsumedLCUs: The number of load balancer capacity units (LCU) used by your load balancer.
  • DesyncMitigationMode_NonCompliant_Request_Count: The number of requests that do not comply with RFC 7230.
  • DroppedInvalidHeaderRequestCount: The number of requests where the load balancer removed HTTP headers with invalid fields before routing the request.
  • MitigatedHostCount: The number of targets under mitigation.
  • ForwardedInvalidHeaderRequestCount: The number of requests routed by the load balancer that had HTTP headers with invalid fields.
  • GrpcRequestCount: The number of gRPC requests processed over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • HTTP_Fixed_Response_Count: The number of successful fixed-response actions.
  • HTTP_Redirect_Count: The number of successful redirect actions.
  • HTTP_Redirect_Url_Limit_Exceeded_Count: The number of redirect actions that failed because the URL in the response location header exceeded 8K.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_3XX_Count: The number of HTTP 3XX redirection codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_4XX_Count: The number of HTTP 4XX client error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count: The number of HTTP 5XX server error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_500_Count: The number of HTTP 500 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_502_Count: The number of HTTP 502 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_503_Count: The number of HTTP 503 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • HTTPCode_ELB_504_Count: The number of HTTP 504 error codes originating from the load balancer.
  • IPv6ProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer over IPv6.
  • IPv6RequestCount: The number of IPv6 requests received by the load balancer.
  • NewConnectionCount: The total number of new TCP connections established from clients to the load balancer and from the load balancer to targets.
  • NonStickyRequestCount: The number of requests where the load balancer chose a new target because it could not use an existing sticky session.
  • ProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • RejectedConnectionCount: The number of connections rejected because the load balancer reached its maximum number of connections.
  • RequestCount: The number of requests processed over IPv4 and IPv6.
  • RuleEvaluations: The number of rules processed by the load balancer, averaged over an hour.
  • HealthyHostCount: The number of targets that are considered healthy.
  • HTTPCode_Target_2XX_Count: The number of HTTP 2XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_3XX_Count: The number of HTTP 3XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_4XX_Count: The number of HTTP 4XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count: The number of HTTP 5XX response codes generated by the targets.
  • RequestCountPerTarget: The average number of requests per target in a target group.
  • TargetConnectionErrorCount: The number of connections that were not successfully established between the load balancer and a target.
  • TargetResponseTime: The time elapsed (in seconds) from when a request leaves the load balancer until the target starts sending response headers.
  • TargetTLSNegotiationErrorCount: The number of TLS connections initiated by the load balancer that did not establish a session with the target.
  • UnHealthyHostCount: The number of targets that are considered unhealthy.
  • HealthyStateDNS: The number of zones that meet the DNS healthy state requirements.
  • HealthyStateRouting: The number of zones that meet the routing healthy state requirements.
  • UnhealthyRoutingRequestCount: The number of requests routed using the routing failover action (fail open).
  • UnhealthyStateDNS: The number of zones that do not meet the DNS healthy state requirements.
  • UnhealthyStateRouting: The number of zones that do not meet the routing healthy state requirements.
  • LambdaInternalError: The number of requests to a Lambda function that failed due to an issue internal to the load balancer or AWS Lambda.
  • LambdaTargetProcessedBytes: The total number of bytes processed by the load balancer for requests to and responses from a Lambda function.
  • LambdaUserError: The number of requests to a Lambda function that failed due to an issue with the Lambda function itself.
  • ELBAuthError: The number of user authentications that could not be completed due to an internal error.
  • ELBAuthFailure: The number of user authentications that could not be completed because the IdP denied access.
  • ELBAuthLatency: The time elapsed (in milliseconds) to query the IdP for the ID token and user info.
  • ELBAuthRefreshTokenSuccess: The number of times the load balancer successfully refreshed user claims using a refresh token.
  • ELBAuthSuccess: The number of successful authentication actions.
  • ELBAuthUserClaimsSizeExceeded: The number of times a configured IdP returned user claims that exceeded 11K bytes in size.

examples.code:
resources:
  webApi:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/index.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
  publicLb:
    type: application-load-balancer
    properties:
      alarms:
        - description: Too many 5xx errors returned by the load balancer

            type: application-load-balancer-custom
            properties:
              # [!code focus-start]
              metric: HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count
              # [!code focus-end]
              threshold: 50
              statistic: sum
              comparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
          evaluation:
            period: 60
            evaluationPeriods: 5
            breachedPeriods: 3
          notificationTargets:
            - type: slack
              properties:
                conversationId: C0123456789
                accessToken: $Secret('slack-bot-token')

properties.longDescription:
The threshold is compared against the calculated value of statistic(METRIC), where:

  • METRIC is the chosen metric.

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.name: enableRemoteSessions
properties.shortDescription: Allow SSH-like access to running containers for debugging.
properties.longDescription: Enables stacktape container:session to open an interactive shell inside the container. Adds a small SSM agent that uses minimal CPU/memory.

properties.name: environment
properties.shortDescription: Environment variables injected into the container at runtime.
properties.longDescription: Use for configuration like API keys, feature flags, or secrets. Variables from connectTo (e.g., STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING) are added automatically.

examples.code:

        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')

properties.name: iamRoleStatements

properties.name: internalHealthCheck

properties.longDescription: If a container fails the health check, it's terminated and replaced automatically.

properties.name: loadBalancing
properties.shortDescription: How traffic reaches your containers. Affects pricing, features, and protocol support.
properties.longDescription:
• http-api-gateway (default): Pay-per-request (~$1/million requests). Best for most apps. Cheapest at low traffic, but costs grow with volume.

  • application-load-balancer: Flat ~$18/month + usage. Required for gradual deployments (deployment), top-level firewalls (useFirewall), and WebSocket support. More cost-effective above ~500k requests/day. AWS Free Tier eligible.

  • network-load-balancer: For non-HTTP traffic (TCP/TLS) like MQTT, game servers, or custom protocols. Requires explicit ports configuration. Does not support CDN, top-level firewall, or gradual deployments.

        properties:

          healthcheckPath: /health

properties.shortDescription: Name of a web-app-firewall resource to protect this service from common web exploits.
properties.longDescription:
Attaches a regional firewall directly to the service's application load balancer. Requires loadBalancing type application-load-balancer.

To protect a CDN-enabled service at CloudFront instead, use cdn.useFirewall with a web-app-firewall resource whose scope is cdn.

examples.code:

    type: web-app-firewall
    properties:
      scope: regional
  apiService:

        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/main.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
      loadBalancing:
        type: application-load-balancer
      # [!code focus-start]
      useFirewall: serviceFirewall
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT
properties.shortDescription: Deploy in private subnets with a static outbound IP via NAT Gateway.
properties.longDescription:
The container won't have a public IP. All outbound traffic routes through a NAT Gateway, giving you a static IP you can whitelist in external services (APIs, payment gateways, etc.).

Configure the number of NAT Gateways in stackConfig.vpc.nat.

Adds cost: NAT Gateway ~$32/month + data processing fees.

      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: connectTo
properties.shortDescription: Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.
properties.longDescription:
List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

  • Grants IAM permissions (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
  • Opens network access (security group rules for databases, Redis)
  • Injects environment variables with connection details: STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]

Example: connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"] gives this workload full access to both resources and injects STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME, etc.

What each resource type provides:

Bucket — read/write/delete objects → NAME, ARN

DynamoDbTable — CRUD + scan/query → NAME, ARN, STREAM_ARN

RelationalDatabase — network access + connection details → CONNECTION_STRING, HOST, PORT. Aurora also gets READER_CONNECTION_STRING, READER_HOST.

MongoDbAtlasCluster — temporary credential-less access → CONNECTION_STRING

RedisCluster — network access → HOST, READER_HOST, PORT

Function — invoke permission → ARN

BatchJob — submit/list/terminate → JOB_DEFINITION_ARN, STATE_MACHINE_ARN

EventBus — publish events → ARN

UserAuthPool — full control → ID, CLIENT_ID, ARN

SqsQueue — send/receive/delete → ARN, NAME, URL

SnsTopic — publish/subscribe → ARN, NAME

UpstashRedis → HOST, PORT, PASSWORD, REST_TOKEN, REST_URL, REDIS_URL

PrivateService → ADDRESS

aws:ses — full SES email sending permissions

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
      # [!code focus-end]
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}

properties.longDescription:

Configure the number of NAT Gateways in stackConfig.vpc.nat.

Adds cost: NAT Gateway ~$32/month + data processing fees.

      # [!code focus-start]
      usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true
      # [!code focus-end]

properties.name: volumeMounts
properties.shortDescription: Persistent EFS volumes shared across containers and restarts.
properties.longDescription: Data stored in EFS volumes persists even when containers are replaced. Multiple containers can mount the same volume. All data is encrypted in transit.

examples.code:
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: stacktape-image-buildpack
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      # [!code focus-start]
      volumeMounts:
        - type: efs
          properties:
            efsFilesystemName: sharedData
            mountPath: /data
      # [!code focus-end]
  sharedData:
    type: efs-filesystem
    properties: {}
